However, since he is already included by the term 'Brahmā', it should be understood that this is unsuitable. And here, the method of application is as follows: having heard that 'Abhibhū is of good complexion and long-lived', one who arouses sensual desire for it conceives of Abhibhū through the conceiving of craving. Furthermore, by a method beginning with, 'Oh, that I might attain companionship with Abhibhū!', one who directs the mind to attain what has not yet been attained also conceives of Abhibhū through the conceiving of craving. But one who places oneself as inferior and Abhibhū as superior conceives of Abhibhū through the conceiving of conceit. It should be understood that one who grasps by the method of 'Abhibhū is permanent, stable,' and so on, conceives of Abhibhū through the conceiving of views. The rest is just as the method stated in the section on Pajāpati.

Bhūtavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the section on what has come to be and so on is finished.

Ākāsānañcāyatanavārādivaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Section on the Base of Infinite Space and So On

4. Evaṃ [V 1.0040] bhagavā paṭipāṭiyā devaloke dassentopi abhibhūvacanena asaññabhavaṃ dassetvā idāni yasmā ayaṃ vaṭṭakathā, suddhāvāsā ca vivaṭṭapakkhe ṭhitā, anāgāmikhīṇāsavā eva hi te devā. Yasmā vā katipayakappasahassāyukā [M 1.0038] te devā, buddhuppādakāleyeva honti. Buddhā pana asaṅkheyepi kappe na uppajjanti, tadā suññāpi sā bhūmi hoti. Rañño khandhāvāraṭṭhānaṃ viya hi buddhānaṃ suddhāvāsabhavo. Te teneva ca kāraṇena viññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsavasenapi na gahitā, sabbakālikā pana imā maññanā. Tasmā tāsaṃ sadāvijjamānabhūmiṃ dassento suddhāvāse atikkamitvā, ākāsānañcāyatanantiādimāha. Tattha ākāsānañcāyatananti tabbhūmikā cattāro kusalavipākakiriyā khandhā. Te ca tatrūpapannāyeva daṭṭhabbā bhavaparicchedakathā ayanti katvā. Esa nayo viññāṇañcāyatanādīsu. Atthayojanā pana catūsupi etesu vāresu abhibhūvāre vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Mānamaññanā cettha pajāpativāre vuttanayenāpi yujjati.

4. Thus the Blessed One, while showing the deva worlds in sequence, showed the non-percipient existence by the term 'Abhibhū'. Now, since this is a discourse on the round of existence, and the Pure Abodes are established on the side of that which is free from the round—for those devas are indeed non-returners and arahants—and since those devas have lifespans of some thousands of aeons and exist only at the time of a Buddha's arising, but Buddhas do not arise even in an incalculable aeon, then that plane is empty. For the Pure Abodes existence is like a king's encampment for the Buddhas. For that very reason, they are not included by way of the stations of consciousness or the abodes of beings. These conceivings, however, are of all times. Therefore, showing a plane that always exists for them, having passed over the Pure Abodes, he said, 'the base of infinite space,' and so on. Therein, 'the base of infinite space' refers to the four aggregates—wholesome, resultant, and functional—belonging to that plane. And these should be understood as pertaining only to those reborn there, this being a discourse on the delimitation of existence. This is the method for the base of infinite consciousness and so on. As for the application of the meaning, in all four of these sections, it should be understood only in the same way as explained in the section on Abhibhū. Here, the conceiving of conceit also fits with the method explained in the section on Pajāpati.

Ākāsānañcāyatanavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Section on the Base of Infinite Space and So On is concluded.

Diṭṭhasutavārādivaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Section on the Seen, Heard, and So On

5. Evaṃ bhūmivisesādinā bhedena vitthāratopi maññanāvatthuṃ dassetvā idāni sabbamaññanāvatthubhūtaṃ sakkāyapariyāpannaṃ tebhūmakadhammabhedaṃ diṭṭhādīhi catūhi saṅgaṇhitvā dassento, diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhatotiādimāha.

5. Thus, having shown the object of conceiving in detail through the classification of special planes and so on, now, wishing to show the classification of phenomena of the three planes—which has become the object of all conceiving and is included in the existing body—by grouping it under the four beginning with 'the seen', he said, 'The seen, from the seen…' and so on.

Tattha diṭṭhanti maṃsacakkhunāpi diṭṭhaṃ, dibbacakkhunāpi diṭṭhaṃ. Rūpāyatanassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Tattha diṭṭhaṃ maññatīti diṭṭhaṃ tīhi maññanāhi maññati. Kathaṃ? Rūpāyatanaṃ subhasaññāya sukhasaññāya ca passanto tattha chandarāgaṃ janeti, taṃ assādeti abhinandati. Vuttampi hetaṃ [P 1.0037] bhagavatā “itthirūpe, bhikkhave, sattā rattā giddhā gadhitā mucchitā ajjhosannā, te dīgharattaṃ socanti itthirūpavasānugā”ti (a. ni. 5.55). Evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. “Iti [V 1.0041] me rūpaṃ siyā anāgatamaddhānanti vā panettha nandiṃ samannāneti, rūpasampadaṃ vā pana ākaṅkhamāno dānaṃ detī”ti vitthāro. Evampi diṭṭhaṃ taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. Attano pana parassa ca rūpasampattiṃ vipattiṃ nissāya mānaṃ janeti. “Imināhaṃ seyyosmī”ti vā “sadisosmī”ti vā “hīnosmī”ti vāti evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ mānamaññanāya maññati. Rūpāyatanaṃ pana niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassatanti maññati, attānaṃ attaniyanti maññati, maṅgalaṃ amaṅgalanti maññati, evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhimaññanāya maññati. Evaṃ diṭṭhaṃ tīhi maññanāhi maññati. Kathaṃ diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati? Rūpasmiṃ attānaṃ [M 1.0039] samanupassananayena maññanto diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati. Yathā vā dhane dhaññe. Evaṃ rūpasmiṃ rāgādayoti maññantopi diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati. Ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiññeva panassa diṭṭhimaññanāya maññite vatthusmiṃ sinehaṃ mānañca uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. Evaṃ diṭṭhasmiṃ maññati. Sesaṃ pathavīvāre vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

Therein, 'seen' refers to what is seen with the physical eye and with the divine eye. This is a designation for the form base. Therein, 'one conceives the seen' means one conceives the seen with three conceivings. How? A worldling, seeing the form base with perceptions of beauty and pleasure, generates strong desire and lust for it, relishes it, and greatly delights in it. For this has been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, beings are impassioned, greedy, infatuated, besotted, and attached to the form of a woman. For a long time, they sorrow, being under the sway of a woman’s form.' Thus, one conceives the seen by the conceiving of craving. The detailed explanation is: '‘May my form be thus in the future,’ or here one brings forth delight, or desiring the perfection of form, one gives gifts.' In this way too, one conceives the seen by the conceiving of craving. Furthermore, based on the success or failure of one’s own or another’s form, one generates conceit: ‘By this I am superior,’ or ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior.’ Thus, one conceives the seen by the conceiving of conceit. Furthermore, one conceives the form base as permanent, stable, and eternal; one conceives it as self or as belonging to self; one conceives it as auspicious or inauspicious. Thus, one conceives the seen by the conceiving of views. In this way, one conceives the seen with three conceivings. How does one conceive in the seen? Conceiving in the manner of viewing self in form, one conceives in the seen. Just as with wealth or grain. Similarly, one who conceives, ‘Lust and so on have arisen in form,’ also conceives in the seen. This is his conceiving of views. Moreover, for him who gives rise to affection and conceit in that very object conceived through the conceiving of views, the conceivings of craving and conceit should also be understood. Thus, one conceives in the seen. The rest should be understood in the same way as explained in the section on the earth element.

Sutanti maṃsasotenapi sutaṃ, dibbasotenapi sutaṃ, saddāyatanassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

'Heard' refers to what is heard with the physical ear and with the divine ear. This is a designation for the sound base.

Mutanti mutvā munitvā ca gahitaṃ, āhacca upagantvāti attho, indriyānaṃ ārammaṇānañca aññamaññasaṃsilese viññātanti vuttaṃ hoti, gandharasaphoṭṭhabbāyatanānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

'Sensed' means what is grasped after having been sensed and cognized. The meaning is 'having struck' and 'having approached'; it is said to be what is cognized through the mutual contact of the faculties and their objects. This is a designation for the bases of smell, taste, and tangible objects.

Viññātanti manasā viññātaṃ, sesānaṃ sattannaṃ āyatanānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ dhammārammaṇassa vā. Idha pana sakkāyapariyāpannameva labbhati. Vitthāro panettha diṭṭhavāre vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

'Cognized' means what is cognized by the mind. This is a designation for the remaining seven bases, or for the mind-object. Here, however, only that which is included in the existing body is obtained. The detailed explanation here should be known by the very method stated in the section on the seen.

Diṭṭhasuttavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the section on the Seen, Heard, and so on is concluded.

Ekattavārādivaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Section Beginning with Unity

6. Evaṃ sabbaṃ sakkāyabhedaṃ diṭṭhādīhi catūhi dassetvā idāni tameva samāpannakavārena ca asamāpannakavārena ca dvidhā dassento ekattaṃ nānattantiādimāha.

6. Having thus shown all the divisions of identity by means of the four beginning with view, etc., now, wishing to show that very division of identity in two ways—by the section concerning one who has attained and by the section concerning one who has not attained—He spoke the words beginning with 'unity and diversity.'

Ekattanti iminā hi samāpannakavāraṃ dasseti. Nānattanti iminā asamāpannakavāraṃ. Tesaṃ [V 1.0042] ayaṃ vacanattho ekabhāvo ekattaṃ. Nānābhāvo nānattanti. Yojanā panettha samāpannakavāraṃ [P 1.0038] catūhi khandhehi, asamāpannakavārañca pañcahi khandhehi bhinditvā “rūpaṃ attato samanupassatī”tiādinā sāsananayena pathavīvārādīsu vuttena ca aṭṭhakathānayena yathānurūpaṃ vīmaṃsitvā veditabbā. Keci pana ekattanti ekattanayaṃ vadanti nānattanti nānattanayaṃ. Apare “ekattasaññī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā, nānattasaññī attā hotī”ti evaṃ diṭṭhābhinivesaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ idha nādhippetattā ayuttameva hoti.

Indeed, by 'unity' He shows the section concerning one who has attained. By 'diversity' He shows the section concerning one who has not attained. This is the meaning of those words: the state of being one is unity; the state of being various is diversity. Herein, the application should be understood by analyzing the section concerning one who has attained by way of the four aggregates, and the section concerning one who has not attained by way of the five aggregates, and by investigating as is suitable in accordance with the canonical method beginning with 'one regards form as self,' etc., and with the commentarial method stated in the sections beginning with the earth element. Some, however, say that 'unity' means the method of unity, and 'diversity' means the method of diversity. Others speak of a tenacious adherence to the view thus: 'The self, having a perception of unity, is without illness after death,' and 'The self, having a perception of diversity, is without illness after death.' All of that, because it is not intended here, is indeed unsuitable.

Evaṃ [M 1.0040] sabbaṃ sakkāyaṃ dvidhā dassetvā idāni tameva ekadhā sampiṇḍetvā dassento sabbaṃ sabbatotiādimāha. Yojanānayo panettha sabbaṃ assādento sabbaṃ taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. “Mayā ete sattā nimmitā”tiādinā nayena attanā nimmitaṃ maññanto sabbaṃ mānamaññanāya maññati. “Sabbaṃ pubbekatakammahetu, sabbaṃ issaranimmānahetu, sabbaṃ ahetuapaccayā, sabbaṃ atthi, sabbaṃ natthī”tiādinā nayena maññanto sabbaṃ diṭṭhimaññanāya maññatīti veditabbo. Kathaṃ sabbasmiṃ maññati? Idhekacco evaṃdiṭṭhiko hoti “mahā me attā”ti. So sabbalokasannivāsaṃ tassokāsabhāvena parikappetvā so kho pana me ayaṃ attā sabbasminti maññati, ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiṃyeva panassa attani sinehaṃ tabbatthukañca mānaṃ uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. Sesaṃ pathavīvāre vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

Having thus shown all identity in two ways, now, wishing to show it summarized as one, He spoke the words beginning with 'all, from all.' Herein, this is the method of application: one who delights in all conceives of all with the conceiving of craving. One who conceives of things as created by oneself, by the method beginning with 'These beings were created by me,' conceives of all with the conceiving of conceit. It should be understood that one who conceives by the method beginning with 'All is caused by past kamma,' 'All is caused by the creation of a supreme being,' 'All is without cause or condition,' 'All exists,' 'All does not exist,' conceives of all with the conceiving of views. How does one conceive 'in all'? Here, a certain person holds the view: 'My self is great.' Having imagined the entire abode of the world as the domain for that self, they conceive: 'This self of mine is in all.' This is their conceiving of views. Moreover, for them who generate affection and conceit based on that very self, the conceivings of craving and conceit should also be understood. The remainder should be understood according to the method stated in the section on the earth element.

Evaṃ sabbaṃ sakkāyaṃ ekadhā dassetvā idāni aparenapi nayena taṃ ekadhā dassento nibbānaṃ nibbānatoti āha. Tattha nibbānanti “yato kho, bho, ayaṃ attā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgibhūto paricāreti. Ettāvatā kho, bho, ayaṃ attā paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ patto hotī”tiādinā nayena pañcadhā āgataṃ paramadiṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tattha nibbānaṃ assādento taṇhāmaññanāya maññati. Tena nibbānena “ahamasmi nibbānaṃ patto”ti mānaṃ janento mānamaññanāya maññati. Anibbānaṃyeva samānaṃ taṃ nibbānato niccādito ca gaṇhanto diṭṭhimaññanāya maññatīti veditabbo.

Having thus shown all identity as one, now, wishing to show it as one by another method as well, He spoke the words beginning with 'Nibbāna, from Nibbāna.' Therein, by 'Nibbāna' should be understood the supreme Nibbāna-in-this-very-life which is mentioned in five ways, by the method beginning with: 'Sirs, when this self is endowed with, possessed of, and indulges in the five strands of sensual pleasure, to that extent, sirs, this self has attained the supreme Nibbāna-in-this-very-life.' Therein, one who delights in that Nibbāna conceives with the conceiving of craving. One who generates conceit by means of that Nibbāna, thinking, 'I have attained Nibbāna,' conceives with the conceiving of conceit. It should be understood that one who, while it is in fact not Nibbāna, grasps it as Nibbāna and as permanent, etc., conceives with the conceiving of views.

Nibbānato pana aññaṃ attānaṃ gahetvā so kho pana me ayaṃ attā imasmiṃ nibbāneti [V 1.0043] maññanto nibbānasmiṃ maññati, ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiṃyeva [P 1.0039] panassa attani sinehaṃ tabbatthukañca mānaṃ uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. Esa nayo nibbānato maññanāyapi. Tatrapi hi nibbānato aññaṃ attānaṃ gahetvā “idaṃ nibbānaṃ, ayaṃ attā, so kho pana me ayaṃ attā ito nibbānato añño”ti maññanto nibbānato maññati, ayamassa diṭṭhimaññanā. Tasmiṃyeva panassa attani sinehaṃ tabbatthukañca mānaṃ uppādayato taṇhāmānamaññanāpi veditabbā. “Aho sukhaṃ mama nibbāna”nti maññanto pana nibbānaṃ meti maññatīti veditabbo. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Ayaṃ panettha anugīti –

But, having taken a self other than Nibbāna and conceiving, 'This self of mine is in this Nibbāna,' one conceives 'in Nibbāna.' This is their conceiving of views. Moreover, for them who generate affection and conceit based on that very self, the conceivings of craving and conceit should also be understood. This is also the method for conceiving 'from Nibbāna.' For there too, having taken a self other than Nibbāna and conceiving, 'This is Nibbāna, this is the self, and this self of mine is other than this Nibbāna,' one conceives 'from Nibbāna.' This is their conceiving of views. Moreover, for them who generate affection and conceit based on that very self, the conceivings of craving and conceit should also be understood. It should be understood that one who conceives, 'Oh, how blissful is my Nibbāna!' conceives of Nibbāna as 'mine.' The remainder is as has been stated. Herein, this is the summary verse:

Yādiso [M 1.0041] esa sakkāyo, tathā naṃ avijānato;

Puthujjanassa sakkāye, jāyanti sabbamaññanā.

Of whatever nature this identity is, for the ordinary person who does not know it as such, all conceivings arise in regard to that identity.

Jeguccho bhiduro cāyaṃ, dukkho apariṇāyako;

Taṃ paccanīkato bālo, gaṇhaṃ gaṇhāti maññanaṃ.

This identity is repulsive, perishable, suffering, and uncontrollable. The fool, grasping it in the opposite way, grasps conceiving.

Subhato sukhato ceva, sakkāyaṃ anupassato;

Salabhasseva aggimhi, hoti taṇhāya maññanā.

For one who regards identity as beautiful and as pleasant, conceiving through craving arises, just like a moth's in a fire.

Niccasaññaṃ adhiṭṭhāya, sampattiṃ tassa passato;

Gūthādī viya gūthasmiṃ, hoti mānena maññanā.

Having established the perception of permanence, for one who sees accomplishment in that, conceiving through conceit arises, like a worm in excrement.

Attā attaniyo meti, passato naṃ abuddhino;

Ādāse viya bondhissa, diṭṭhiyā hoti maññanā.

For the unwise one who sees it as 'self' and 'mine,' conceiving through views arises, like a fool's reflection in a mirror.

Maññanāti ca nāmetaṃ, sukhumaṃ mārabandhanaṃ;

Sithilaṃ duppamuñcañca, yena baddho puthujjano.

This, which is named 'conceiving,' is a subtle bond of Māra; it is loose and hard to release, and by it the ordinary person is bound.

Bahuṃ [V 1.0044] vipphandamānopi, sakkāyaṃ nātivattati;

Samussitaṃ daḷhatthambhaṃ, sāva gaddulabandhano.

Though struggling much, one does not overcome identity, like a dog bound by a leash to a firmly planted, strong post.

Sa’so sakkāyamalīno, jātiyā ca jarāya ca;

Rogādīhi ca dukkhehi, niccaṃ haññati bāḷhaso.

That person, defiled by identity, is always severely afflicted by birth, aging, and by sufferings such as disease.

Taṃ vo vadāmi bhaddante, sakkāyaṃ anupassatha;

Asātato asubhato, bhedato ca anattato.

Therefore, I say to you, venerable sirs: contemplate identity as unpleasant, as impure, as perishable, and as not-self.

Eso sabhāvo hetassa, passaṃ evamimaṃ budho;

Pahāya maññanā sabbā, sabbadukkhā pamuccatīti.

This is its nature. The wise person, seeing it thus, having abandoned all conceivings, is freed from all suffering.

Ekattavārādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Section Beginning with Unity is completed.

Puthujjanavasena [P 1.0040] catuvīsatipabbā paṭhamanayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The first exposition of method, with its twenty-four divisions concerning the ordinary person, is completed.

Sekkhavāradutiyanayavaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Second Method concerning the Trainee.

7. Evaṃ [M 1.0042] bhagavā pathavīādīsu vatthūsu sabbasakkāyadhammamūlabhūtaṃ puthujjanassa pavattiṃ dassetvā idāni tesveva vatthūsu sekkhassa pavattiṃ dassento yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekkhotiādimāha. Tattha yoti uddesavacanaṃ. Soti niddesavacanaṃ. Pikāro sampiṇḍanattho ayampi dhammo aniyatotiādīsu viya. Tena ca ārammaṇasabhāgena puggalaṃ sampiṇḍeti, no puggalasabhāgena, heṭṭhato hi puggalā diṭṭhivipannā, idha diṭṭhisampannā, na tesaṃ sabhāgatā atthi. Ārammaṇaṃ pana heṭṭhā puggalānampi tadeva, imesampi tadevāti. Tena vuttaṃ “ārammaṇasabhāgena puggalaṃ sampiṇḍeti no puggalasabhāgenā”ti. Yopi soti iminā pana sakalena vacanena idāni vattabbaṃ sekkhaṃ dassetīti veditabbo. Bhikkhave, bhikkhūti idaṃ vuttanayameva.

7. Thus, the Blessed One, having shown the occurrence of the ordinary person, which is the root of all phenomena of personal identity, in things such as earth, now, wishing to show the occurrence of a trainee in those very same things, says, “And whichever bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is a trainee,” and so on. Therein, ‘yo’ is a term of designation; ‘so’ is a term of specification. The particle ‘pi’ has the meaning of aggregation, as in ‘this phenomenon too is undetermined,’ and so on. And by it, one aggregates the person by means of the shared object, not by means of shared personhood. For, in the preceding section, the persons are corrupt in view, while here they are accomplished in view—there is no commonality between them. The object, however, is the same for the persons in the preceding section and for these here. Therefore, it is said: “One aggregates the person by means of the shared object, not by means of shared personhood.” By this entire phrase ‘yopi so,’ it should be understood that it now indicates the trainee who is to be spoken of. The phrase ‘Bhikkhave, bhikkhu’ is in the same manner as previously stated.

Sekkhoti [V 1.0045] kenaṭṭhena sekkho? Sekkhadhammappaṭilābhato sekkho. Vuttañhetaṃ “kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sekkho hotīti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekkhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti…pe… sekkhena sammāsamādhinā samannāgato hoti. Ettāvatā kho bhikkhu, sekkho hotī”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.13). Apica sikkhatītipi sekkho. Vuttañhetaṃ “sikkhatīti kho bhikkhu tasmā sekkhoti vuccati. Kiñca sikkhati? Adhisīlampi sikkhati, adhicittampi sikkhati, adhipaññampi sikkhati, sikkhatīti kho bhikkhu tasmā sekkhoti vuccatī”ti (a. ni. 3.86).

‘A trainee’: in what sense is one a trainee? One is a trainee by virtue of having attained the qualities of a trainee. For this has been said: ‘To what extent, venerable sir, is one a trainee? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with the trainee’s right view… endowed with the trainee’s right concentration. To this extent, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is a trainee.’ Furthermore, one is also a trainee because one trains. For this has been said: ‘Because he trains, bhikkhu, he is therefore called a trainee. And what does he train in? He trains in higher virtue, he trains in higher mind, he trains in higher wisdom. Because he trains, bhikkhu, he is therefore called a trainee.’

Yopi kalyāṇaputhujjano anulomapaṭipadāya paripūrakārī sīlasampanno indriyesu guttadvāro bhojane mattaññū jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto pubbarattāpararattaṃ bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto viharati – “ajja vā sve vā aññataraṃ sāmaññaphalaṃ adhigamissāmī”ti, sopi vuccati sikkhatīti sekkhoti. Imasmiṃ panatthe paṭivedhappattova sekkho adhippeto, no puthujjano.

And also a virtuous ordinary person who is a fulfiller of the practice that is in conformity, is accomplished in virtue, has guarded sense-faculties, knows the measure in eating, is devoted to the practice of wakefulness, and dwells devoted to the practice of cultivating the factors of enlightenment during the first and last watches of the night, thinking, ‘Today or tomorrow I will realize one of the fruits of asceticism’—he too is called a ‘trainee’ because he trains. In this context, however, only a trainee who has attained penetration is intended, not an ordinary person.

Appattaṃ mānasaṃ etenāti appattamānaso. Mānasanti rāgopi cittampi arahattampi. “Antalikkhacaro pāso, yvāyaṃ [P 1.0041] carati mānaso”ti (mahāva. 33; saṃ. ni. 1.151) ettha hi rāgo [M 1.0043] mānasaṃ. “Cittaṃ mano mānasa”nti (dha. sa. 65) ettha cittaṃ. “Appattamānaso sekkho, kālaṃ kayirā janesutā”ti (saṃ. ni. 1.159) ettha arahattaṃ. Idhāpi arahattameva adhippetaṃ. Tena appattārahattoti vuttaṃ hoti.

‘Appattamānaso’ means one by whom the goal (mānasa) has not been attained. ‘Mānasa’ can mean lust, mind, or Arahantship. For in the passage, “A snare that roams in the sky, this mānasa that wanders,” ‘mānasa’ means lust. In the passage, “Cittaṃ, mano, mānasaṃ,” it means mind. In the passage, “A trainee with mānasa unattained, were he to pass away, O leader of men,” it means Arahantship. Here too, Arahantship alone is intended. Therefore, it means ‘one who has not attained Arahantship.’”

Anuttaranti seṭṭhaṃ, asadisanti attho. Catūhi yogehi khemaṃ ananuyuttanti yogakkhemaṃ, arahattameva adhippetaṃ. Patthayamānoti dve patthanā taṇhāpatthanā ca, chandapatthanā ca. “Patthayamānassa hi pajappitāni, pavedhitaṃ vāpi pakappitesū”ti (su. ni. 908) ettha taṇhāpatthanā.

‘Anuttaraṃ’ (unexcelled) means supreme, incomparable. ‘Yogakkhemaṃ’ (security from the yokes) means security from the four yokes, not being yoked to them; Arahantship alone is intended. ‘Patthayamāno’ (aspiring): there are two kinds of aspiration—aspiration as craving and aspiration as wholesome desire. In the passage, “For one who aspires, there are fancies and agitation regarding what has been imagined,” aspiration as craving is meant.

“Chinnaṃ pāpimato sotaṃ, viddhastaṃ vinaḷīkataṃ;

Pāmojjabahulā hotha, khemaṃ pattattha bhikkhavo”ti. (ma. ni. 1.352) –

In the passage: “The stream of the Evil One is cut, shattered, and rendered harmless. Be full of joy, O bhikkhus; aspire to security!”

Ettha [V 1.0046] kattukamyatā kusalacchandapatthanā. Ayameva idhādhippetā. Tena patthayamānoti taṃ yogakkhemaṃ pattukāmo adhigantukāmo tanninno tappoṇo tappabbhāroti veditabbo. Viharatīti aññaṃ iriyāpathadukkhaṃ aññena iriyāpathena vicchinditvā aparipatantaṃ kāyaṃ harati. Atha vā “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccāti adhimuccanto saddhāya viharatī”tiādināpi niddesanayenettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Pathaviṃ pathavito abhijānātīti pathaviṃ pathavībhāvena abhijānāti, na puthujjano viya sabbākāraviparītāya saññāya sañjānāti. Apica kho abhivisiṭṭhena ñāṇena jānāti, evaṃ pathavīti etaṃ pathavībhāvaṃ adhimuccanto eva naṃ aniccātipi dukkhātipi anattātipi evaṃ abhijānātīti vuttaṃ hoti. Evañca naṃ abhiññatvā pathaviṃ mā maññīti vuttaṃ hoti. Maññatīti maññi. Ayaṃ pana maññī ca na maññī ca na vattabboti. Etasmiñhi atthe idaṃ padaṃ nipātetvā vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Ko panettha adhippāyoti. Vuccate, puthujjano [P 1.0042] tāva sabbamaññanānaṃ appahīnattā maññatīti vutto. Khīṇāsavo pahīnattā na maññatīti. Sekkhassa pana diṭṭhimaññanā pahīnā, itarā pana tanubhāvaṃ gatā, tena so maññatītipi na vattabbo puthujjano viya, na maññatītipi na vattabbo khīṇāsavo viyāti.

Here, the wholesome aspiration of the desire to act is intended. This very aspiration is intended here. Therefore, ‘aspiring’ should be understood as desiring to attain that security from the yokes, being eager to realize it, inclined towards it, tending towards it, gravitating towards it. ‘He dwells’ means he carries on the body without letting it fall, interrupting the discomfort of one posture with another. Or, the meaning here should also be seen according to the method of exposition beginning with, “He dwells with faith, resolving, ‘All conditioned things are impermanent.’” ‘He directly knows earth as earth’ means he directly knows earth by way of its earth-nature; he does not know it like an ordinary person with a perception that is distorted in every way. Rather, he knows it with a superior knowledge. It is meant that he knows it only by resolving on this nature of earth as something to be directly known; he does not directly know it as ‘impermanent,’ ‘suffering,’ or ‘non-self.’ And having thus directly known it, it is meant, ‘Do not conceive of earth.’ ‘Maññi’ comes from ‘maññati’ (he conceives). It should be understood that in this sense, this word is stated with an elision. But of this one, it cannot be said that ‘he conceives’ nor that ‘he does not conceive.’ What is the intention here? It is said: An ordinary person, because all conceivings are unabandoned, is said to ‘conceive.’ One whose cankers are destroyed, because they are abandoned, is said to ‘not conceive.’ As for the trainee, however, the conceiving of views is abandoned, while the other conceivings have become attenuated. Therefore, it cannot be said of him that he ‘conceives’ like an ordinary person, nor that he ‘does not conceive’ like one whose cankers are destroyed.

Pariññeyyaṃ tassāti tassa sekkhassa taṃ maññanāvatthu okkantaniyāmattā sambodhiparāyaṇattā ca tīhi pariññāhi pariññeyyaṃ, apariññeyyañca apariññātañca [M 1.0044] na hoti puthujjanassa viya, nopi pariññātaṃ khīṇāsavassa viya. Sesaṃ sabbattha vuttanayameva.

‘It is to be fully understood by him’ means that for that trainee, that object of conceiving is to be fully understood by the three kinds of full understanding, because he has entered the fixed course and is bound for enlightenment. It is not ‘not-to-be-fully-understood’ nor ‘not-yet-fully-understood’ as it is for an ordinary person; nor is it ‘fully understood’ as it is for one whose cankers are destroyed. The rest is in the same manner as stated everywhere.

Sekkhavasena dutiyanayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the second method concerning the trainee is concluded.

Khīṇāsavavāratatiyādinayavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Method beginning with the Third Section on the One Whose Taints are Destroyed

8. Evaṃ pathavīādīsu vatthūsu sekkhassa pavattiṃ dassetvā idāni khīṇāsavassa pavattiṃ dassento yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahantiādimāha. Tattha yopīti pi-saddo sampiṇḍanattho. Tena idha ubhayasabhāgatāpi labbhatīti dasseti. Sekkho hi khīṇāsavena ariyapuggalattā sabhāgo, tena puggalasabhāgatā labbhati, ārammaṇasabhāgatā pana vuttanayā eva. Arahanti ārakakileso, dūrakileso pahīnakilesoti attho. Vuttañcetaṃ bhagavatā “kathañca[V 1.0047], bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ hoti? Ārakāssa honti pāpakā akusalā dhammā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ hotī”ti. (Ma. ni. 1.434) khīṇāsavoti cattāro āsavā kāmāsavo…pe… avijjāsavo, ime cattāro āsavā arahato khīṇā pahīnā samucchinnā paṭippassaddhā, abhabbuppattikā ñāṇagginā daḍḍhā, tena vuccati khīṇāsavoti.

8. Having thus shown the occurrence in a learner regarding objects such as the earth element, now, wishing to show the occurrence in one whose taints are destroyed, the Blessed One said, 'Whatever monk, bhikkhus, is an Arahant…' and so on. Therein, in the phrase 'yopi', the particle 'pi' has the meaning of combination. By this, it is shown that here a twofold commonality is obtained. Indeed, a learner is similar to one whose taints are destroyed because of being a noble person; by that, commonality of person is obtained. Commonality of object, however, is just as was explained. 'Arahant' means one whose defilements are far, whose defilements are distant, one whose defilements are abandoned. And this was said by the Blessed One: 'And how, bhikkhus, is a monk an Arahant? Evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, accompanied by distress, ripening in suffering, and leading to future birth, aging, and death are far from him. Thus, bhikkhus, a monk is an Arahant.' 'One whose taints are destroyed' means: the four taints—the taint of sensual desire… and so on… the taint of ignorance. For an Arahant, these four taints are destroyed, abandoned, severed, calmed, made incapable of arising again, and burned by the fire of knowledge. Therefore, he is called 'one whose taints are destroyed.'

Vusitavāti garusaṃvāsepi ariyamaggasaṃvāsepi dasasu ariyavāsesupi vasi parivasi vuttho parivuttho, so vutthavāso ciṇṇacaraṇoti vusitavā katakaraṇīyoti puthujjanakalyāṇakaṃ upādāya satta sekkhā catūhi maggehi karaṇīyaṃ karonti nāma, khīṇāsavassa sabbakaraṇīyāni katāni pariyositāni, natthi tassa uttari karaṇīyaṃ dukkhakkhayādhigamāyāti katakaraṇīyo. Vuttampi hetaṃ –

‘He has lived the life’ means: he has dwelt and thoroughly dwelt in the living in dependence on a teacher, in the living of the Noble Path, and in the ten Noble Abidings; that living has been completed, that conduct has been practiced, therefore he is called ‘one who has lived the life’. ‘One whose task is done’ means: beginning with the virtuous worldling, the seven learners are said to be doing what is to be done by means of the four paths. For one whose taints are destroyed, all tasks to be done have been done, have been completed. For him, there is nothing further to be done for the attainment of the destruction of suffering; therefore, he is called ‘one whose task is done’. And this has been said:

“Tassa [P 1.0043] sammā vimuttassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno;

Katassa paṭicayo natthi, karaṇīyaṃ na vijjatī”ti. (theragā. 642);

“For that monk who is rightly freed, whose mind is at peace, there is no accumulation for what has been done, and nothing further to be done is found.”

Ohitabhāroti tayo bhārā khandhabhāro kilesabhāro abhisaṅkhārabhāroti, tassime tayo bhārā ohitā oropitā nikkhittā [M 1.0045] pātitā, tena vuccati ohitabhāroti. Anuppattasadatthoti anuppatto sadatthaṃ, sakatthanti vuttaṃ hoti. Kakārassāyaṃ dakāro kato, sadatthoti ca arahattaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tañhi attupanibandhanaṭṭhena attānaṃ avijahanaṭṭhena attano paramatthaṭṭhena ca attano attho sakatthoti vuccati.

‘One who has laid down the burden’ means: there are three burdens—the burden of the aggregates, the burden of defilements, and the burden of formations. For that Arahant, these three burdens are laid down and relinquished. Therefore, he is called ‘one who has laid down the burden’. ‘One who has attained one's own goal’ means: one has attained one's own goal, which is to say, one's own benefit. Here, for the letter 'k', the letter 'd' has been made. And by 'one's own goal' (sadattha), Arahantship should be understood. Indeed, that is called 'one's own benefit' (sakattha) because it is connected to oneself, because it does not abandon oneself, and because it is one's own ultimate goal.

Parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanoti bhavasaṃyojanānīti dasa saṃyojanāni kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ paṭighamānadiṭṭhivicikicchāsīlabbataparāmāsabhavarāgaissāmacchariyasaṃyojanaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ. Imāni hi satte bhavesu saṃyojenti upanibandhanti, bhavaṃ vā bhavena saṃyojenti, tasmā “bhavasaṃyojanānī”ti vuccanti. Imāni bhavasaṃyojanāni arahato parikkhīṇāni pahīnāni ñāṇagginā daḍḍhāni, tena vuccati “parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano”ti. Sammadaññā vimuttoti ettha sammadaññāti sammā aññāya. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti – khandhānaṃ khandhaṭṭhaṃ, āyatanānaṃ āyatanaṭṭhaṃ, dhātūnaṃ [V 1.0048] dhātuṭṭhaṃ, dukkhassa pīḷanaṭṭhaṃ, samudayassa pabhavaṭṭhaṃ, nirodhassa santaṭṭhaṃ, maggassa dassanaṭṭhaṃ, sabbe saṅkhārā aniccāti evamādiṃ vā bhedaṃ sammā yathābhūtaṃ aññāya jānitvā tīrayitvā tulayitvā vibhāvetvā vibhūtaṃ katvāti.

‘One whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed’: ‘Fetters of existence’ means the ten fetters: the fetter of sensual desire, the fetter of ill will, conceit, view, doubt, attachment to rites and rituals, craving for existence, envy, stinginess, and the fetter of ignorance. These indeed bind beings in existences, they tie them down; or they bind one existence with another. Therefore, they are called ‘fetters of existence’. For an Arahant, these fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, abandoned, and burned by the fire of knowledge. Therefore, he is called ‘one whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed’. ‘Liberated through right, full knowledge’: Herein, ‘sammadaññā’ means ‘having rightly known’. What is meant? Having known the meaning of the aggregates as aggregates, the meaning of the sense bases as sense bases, the meaning of the elements as elements, the meaning of suffering as oppression, the meaning of the origin as its source, the meaning of cessation as peace, the meaning of the path as seeing; or, having known the classification beginning with ‘all formations are impermanent’ rightly and as it really is, having investigated, weighed, made manifest, and made clear. Thus it is meant.

Vimuttoti dve vimuttiyo cittassa ca vimutti nibbānañca. Arahā sabbakilesehi vimuttacittattā cittavimuttiyāpi vimutto. Nibbānaṃ adhimuttattā nibbānepi vimutto. Tena vuccati “sammadaññā vimutto”ti. Pariññātaṃ tassāti tassa arahato taṃ maññanāvatthu tīhi pariññāhi pariññātaṃ. Tasmā so taṃ vatthuṃ na maññati, taṃ vā maññanaṃ na maññatīti vuttaṃ hoti, sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

‘Liberated’: There are two liberations: the liberation of the mind and Nibbāna. An Arahant, because his mind is liberated from all defilements, is liberated by the liberation of the mind. Because he is intent on Nibbāna, he is also liberated in regard to Nibbāna. Therefore, he is called ‘liberated through right, full knowledge’. ‘It is fully known by him’ means: for that Arahant, that object of conceiving is fully known through the three kinds of full understanding. Therefore, it is meant that he does not conceive that object, or he does not engage in that conceiving. The rest is just as has been explained.

Nibbānavāre [P 1.0044] pana khayā rāgassātiādayo tayo vārā vuttā. Te pathavīvārādīsupi vitthāretabbā. Ayañca pariññātavāro nibbānavārepi vitthāretabbo. Vitthārentena ca pariññātaṃ tassāti sabbapadehi yojetvā puna khayā rāgassa vītarāgattāti yojetabbaṃ. Esa nayo itaresu. Desanā pana ekattha vuttaṃ sabbattha vuttameva hotīti saṃkhittā.

However, in the section on Nibbāna, three sections beginning with ‘due to the destruction of lust’ are stated. These should be elaborated also in the sections beginning with the earth section. And this section on full understanding should also be elaborated in the section on Nibbāna. When elaborating, the phrase ‘it is fully known by him’ should be connected with all the terms, and then the phrase ‘due to the destruction of lust, being free from lust’ should be connected. This is the method for the remaining sections. The teaching, however, when stated in one place is in fact stated everywhere; for this reason, it is presented in brief.

Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattāti ettha ca yasmā bāhirako kāmesu vītarāgo, na khayā rāgassa vītarāgo. Arahā pana khayā yeva, tasmā vuttaṃ [M 1.0046] “khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā”ti. Esa nayo dosamohesupi. Yathā ca “pariññātaṃ tassāti vadāmī”ti vuttepi pariññātattā so taṃ vatthuṃ taṃ vā maññanaṃ na maññatīti attho hoti, evamidhāpi vītarāgattā so taṃ vatthuṃ taṃ vā maññanaṃ na maññatīti daṭṭhabbo.

And here, in the phrase ‘due to the destruction of lust, being free from lust’: Because an outsider, though free from lust regarding sensual pleasures (through suppression), is not free from lust through the destruction of lust. An Arahant, however, is free from lust precisely through its destruction. Therefore, it is said, ‘due to the destruction of lust, being free from lust’. This is the method for hatred and delusion as well. And just as when it is said, ‘I say: It is fully known by him,’ the meaning is that because it is fully known, he does not conceive that object, nor does that conceiving occur; so too here, it should be understood that because of being free from lust, he does not conceive that object, nor does that conceiving occur.

Ettha ca pariññātaṃ tassāti ayaṃ vāro maggabhāvanāpāripūridassanatthaṃ vutto. Itare pana phalasacchikiriyāpāripūridassanatthanti veditabbā. Dvīhi vā kāraṇehi arahā na maññati vatthussa ca pariññātattā akusalamūlānañca samucchinnattā. Tenassa pariññātavārena vatthuno vatthupariññaṃ dīpeti, itarehi akusalamūlasamucchedanti. Tattha pacchimesu tīsu vāresu ayaṃ viseso veditabbo, tīsu hi vāresu rāge ādīnavaṃ disvā dukkhānupassī viharanto appaṇihitavimokkhena vimutto khayā rāgassa vītarāgo hoti. Dose ādīnavaṃ disvā aniccānupassī [V 1.0049] viharanto animittavimokkhena vimutto khayā dosassa vītadoso hoti. Mohe ādīnavaṃ disvā anattānupassī viharanto suññatavimokkhena vimutto khayā mohassa vītamoho hotīti.

And here, this section 'it is fully understood by him' is stated to show the completion of the development of the path. The others, however, should be understood as for the purpose of showing the completion of the realization of the fruit. Or, an Arahant does not conceive for two reasons: because the basis has been fully understood and because the unwholesome roots have been eradicated. By that section on full understanding, it shows the full understanding of the basis for him; by the others, it shows the eradication of the unwholesome roots. In this context, this distinction in the last three sections should be understood: in these three sections, one who, having seen the danger in greed, abides contemplating suffering, is liberated by the desireless liberation; through the destruction of greed, he becomes free from greed. One who, having seen the danger in hatred, abides contemplating impermanence, is liberated by the signless liberation; through the destruction of hatred, he becomes free from hatred. One who, having seen the danger in delusion, abides contemplating not-self, is liberated by the emptiness liberation; through the destruction of delusion, he becomes free from delusion.

Evaṃ sante na eko tīhi vimokkhehi vimuccatīti dve vārā na vattabbā siyunti ce, taṃ na. Kasmā? Aniyamitattā. Aniyamena hi vuttaṃ “yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araha”nti. Na pana vuttaṃ appaṇihitavimokkhena vā vimutto, itarena vāti, tasmā yaṃ arahato yujjati, taṃ sabbaṃ vattabbamevāti.

If it is said: 'This being so, since one is not liberated by three liberations, the two sections should not be stated,' that is not so. Why? Because it is unfixed. For it was said without restriction: 'That monk, bhikkhus, who is an Arahant...' But it was not said that he was liberated by the desireless liberation or by another. Therefore, whatever is fitting for an Arahant, all of that should indeed be stated.

Avisesena vā yo koci arahā samānepi rāgādikkhaye vipariṇāmadukkhassa pariññātattā khayā rāgassa vītarāgoti vuccati, dukkhadukkhassa pariññātattā khayā dosassa vītadosoti. Saṅkhāradukkhassa pariññātattā khayā mohassa vītamohoti. Iṭṭhārammaṇassa vā pariññātattā khayā rāgassa vītarāgo. Aniṭṭhārammaṇassa pariññātattā khayā dosassa vītadoso. Majjhattārammaṇassa pariññātattā [P 1.0045] khayā mohassa vītamoho. Sukhāya vā vedanāya rāgānusayassa samucchinnattā khayā rāgassa vītarāgo, itarāsu paṭighamohānusayānaṃ samucchinnattā [M 1.0047] vītadoso vītamoho cāti. Tasmā taṃ visesaṃ dassento āha “khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā…pe… vītamohattā”ti.

Or, without distinction, any Arahant whatsoever, even though the destruction of lust, etc., is the same, is, because of having fully understood the suffering of change, called 'one free from lust through the destruction of lust.' Because of having fully understood suffering as pain, he is called 'one free from hatred through the destruction of hatred.' Because of having fully understood the suffering of conditioned formations, he is called 'one free from delusion through the destruction of delusion.' Or, because of having fully understood a desirable object, he is called 'one free from lust through the destruction of lust.' Because of having fully understood an undesirable object, he is called 'one free from hatred through the destruction of hatred.' Because of having fully understood a neutral object, he is called 'one free from delusion through the destruction of delusion.' Or, because the underlying tendency to lust in regard to pleasant feeling has been eradicated, he is called 'one free from lust through the destruction of lust'; and because the underlying tendencies to aversion and delusion in regard to the other feelings have been eradicated, he is called 'one free from hatred' and 'one free from delusion.' Therefore, showing that distinction, He said: 'because of being free from lust through the destruction of lust... because of being free from delusion.'

Khīṇāsavavasena tatiyacatutthapañcamachaṭṭhanayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth methods, by way of the one whose taints are destroyed, is finished.

Tathāgatavārasattamanayavaṇṇanā

The explanation of the seventh method in the section on the Tathāgata.

12. Evaṃ pathavīādīsu vatthūsu khīṇāsavassa pavattiṃ dassetvā idāni attano pavattiṃ dassento tathāgatopi, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha tathāgatoti aṭṭhahi kāraṇehi bhagavā tathāgatoti vuccati – tathā āgatoti tathāgato, tathā gatoti tathāgato, tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgatoti tathāgato, tathadhamme yāthāvato abhisambuddhoti tathāgato, tathadassitāya tathāgato, tathāvāditāya tathāgato, tathākāritāya tathāgato, abhibhavanaṭṭhena tathāgatoti.

Having thus shown the mode of being of one whose taints are destroyed in regard to objects such as the earth element, the Blessed One, now wishing to show His own mode of being, spoke the words beginning with 'The Tathāgata also, Bhikkhus...'. Therein, the Blessed One is called 'Tathāgata' for eight reasons: because He has come in the same way (tathā āgato); because He has gone in the same way (tathā gato); because He has arrived at the true characteristic (tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgato); because He has fully awakened to the true phenomena as they are (tathadhamme yāthāvato abhisambuddho); because He sees what is true (tathadassitāya); because He speaks what is true (tathāvāditāya); because He does what is true (tathākāritāya); and by the meaning of overcoming (abhibhavanaṭṭhena).

Kathaṃ [V 1.0050] bhagavā tathā āgatoti tathāgato? Yathā sabbalokahitāya ussukkamāpannā purimakā sammāsambuddhā āgatā, yathā vipassī bhagavā āgato, yathā sikhī bhagavā, yathā vessabhū bhagavā, yathā kakusandho bhagavā, yathā koṇāgamano bhagavā, yathā kassapo bhagavā āgatoti. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Yena abhinīhārena ete bhagavanto āgatā, teneva amhākampi bhagavā āgato.

12. How is the Blessed One a Tathāgata, 'one who has come in the same way'? Just as the previous Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones came, having undertaken the endeavor for the welfare of the whole world—as the Blessed One Vipassī came, as the Blessed One Sikhī, as the Blessed One Vessabhū, as the Blessed One Kakusandha, as the Blessed One Koṇāgamana, as the Blessed One Kassapa came. What is meant by this? Our Blessed One has also come with the same aspiration with which those Blessed Ones came.

Atha vā yathā vipassī bhagavā…pe… yathā kassapo bhagavā dānapāramiṃ pūretvā, sīlanekkhammapaññāvīriyakhantisaccaadhiṭṭhānamettāupekkhāpāramiṃ pūretvā, imā dasa pāramiyo, dasa upapāramiyo, dasa paramatthapāramiyoti, samatiṃsa pāramiyo pūretvā, aṅgapariccāgaṃ nayanadhanarajjaputtadārapariccāganti ime pañca mahāpariccāge pariccajitvā pubbayogapubbacariyadhammakkhānañātatthacariyādayo pūretvā, buddhicariyāya koṭiṃ patvā āgato, tathā amhākampi bhagavā āgato.

Or else, just as the Blessed One Vipassī... up to the Blessed One Kassapa, having fulfilled the perfection of generosity, and having fulfilled the perfections of virtue, renunciation, wisdom, energy, patience, truthfulness, determination, loving-kindness, and equanimity—these ten perfections, ten secondary perfections, and ten ultimate perfections—thus fulfilling the thirty perfections, having relinquished the five great relinquishments—the giving up of limbs, eyes, wealth, kingdom, sons, and wife—having fulfilled former endeavors, former conduct, the exposition of the Dhamma, conduct for the benefit of relatives, and so on, having reached the culmination of the conduct for Buddhahood, He came; in the same way, our Blessed One has also come.

Yathā ca vipassī bhagavā…pe… yathā kassapo bhagavā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne sammappadhāne iddhipāde pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅge ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvetvā brūhetvā āgato, tathā amhākaṃ [P 1.0046] bhagavāpi āgatoti tathāgato.

And just as the Blessed One Vipassī... up to the Blessed One Kassapa, having developed and cultivated the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the Noble Eightfold Path, came, so too our Blessed One has come. Thus, He is called 'Tathāgata'.

Yatheva [M 1.0048] lokamhi vipassiādayo,

Sabbaññubhāvaṃ munayo idhāgatā;

Tathā ayaṃ sakyamunīpi āgato,

Tathāgato vuccati tena cakkhumāti.

Just as in the world sages such as Vipassī came, having attained omniscience, so too has this Sakyan Sage come; therefore, He, the One with Vision, is called 'Tathāgata'.

Evaṃ tathā āgatoti tathāgato.

Thus, He is called 'Tathāgata' because He has come in the same way.

Kathaṃ tathā gatoti tathāgato. Yathā sampatijāto vipassī bhagavā gato…pe… kassapo bhagavā gato. Kathañca so gatoti, so hi sampatijātova samehi pādehi pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya uttarābhimukho sattapadavītihārena gato. Yathāha – sampatijāto, ānanda, bodhisatto samehi [V 1.0051] pādehi pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhahitvā uttarābhimukho sattapadavītihārena gacchati setamhi chatte anudhārīyamāne, sabbā ca disā anuviloketi, āsabhiñca vācaṃ bhāsati “aggohamasmi lokassa, jeṭṭhohamasmi lokassa, seṭṭhohamasmi lokassa, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti (ma. ni. 3.207).

How is He a 'Tathāgata' because He has gone in the same way (tathā gato)? Just as the Blessed One Vipassī went, immediately upon being born... up to the Blessed One Kassapa went. And how did He go? Immediately upon being born, standing firmly on the earth with even feet, facing north, He went, taking seven steps. As it is said: 'Ānanda, the Bodhisatta, immediately upon being born, stands firmly on the earth with even feet, faces north, and takes seven steps while a white parasol is held over him. He surveys all directions and utters a bull-like utterance: "I am the chief in the world, I am the eldest in the world, I am the foremost in the world. This is my last birth; now there is no further becoming."' (MN 3.207).

Tañcassa gamanaṃ tathaṃ ahosi avitathaṃ anekesaṃ visesādhigamānaṃ pubbanimittabhāvena. Yañhi so sampatijātova samehi pādehi patiṭṭhahi, idamassa caturiddhipādapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ. Uttarābhimukhabhāvo pana sabbalokuttarabhāvassa pubbanimittaṃ. Sattapadavītihāro sattabojjhaṅgaratanapaṭilābhassa. “Suvaṇṇadaṇḍā vītipatanti cāmarā”ti (su. ni. 693) ettha vutto cāmarukkhepo sabbatitthiyanimmathanassa. Setacchattadhāraṇaṃ arahattavimuttivaravimalasetacchattapaṭilābhassa. Sabbadisānuvilokanaṃ sabbaññutānāvaraṇañāṇapaṭilābhassa. Āsabhīvācābhāsanaṃ appaṭivattiyavaradhammacakkappavattanassa pubbanimittaṃ. Tathā ayaṃ bhagavāpi gato. Tañcassa gamanaṃ tathaṃ ahosi avitathaṃ tesaññeva visesādhigamānaṃ pubbanimittabhāvena. Tenāhu porāṇā –

And that going of his was true, not false, being a preliminary sign for the attainment of many special qualities. For that he stood firmly with even feet just after being born—this was a preliminary sign for his attainment of the four bases of psychic power. His facing northward was a preliminary sign for his attainment of a state supreme in all the world. His striding seven steps was for the attainment of the seven jewel-like factors of enlightenment. The raising of the chowries, mentioned in the verse, “Golden-handled chowries wave to and fro,” was for the crushing of all sectarians. The holding of the white parasol was for the attainment of the excellent, immaculate, white parasol of the liberation of Arahantship. His looking around in all directions was for the attainment of the unobstructed knowledge of omniscience. His uttering a bull-like cry was a preliminary sign for the turning of the excellent, irreversible Wheel of Dhamma. In the same way, this Blessed One also went. And that going of his was true, not false, being a preliminary sign for the attainment of those very same special qualities. Therefore, the ancients said:

“Muhuttajātova gavampatī yathā,

Samehi pādehi phusī vasundharaṃ;

So vikkamī satta padāni gotamo,

Setañca chattaṃ anudhārayuṃ marū.

Just as the lord of the herd, at the moment of birth, touched the earth with even feet; so Gotama strode seven steps, and the gods held up a white parasol.

Gantvāna [M 1.0049][P 1.0047] so satta padāni gotamo,

Disā vilokesi samā samantato;

Aṭṭhaṅgupetaṃ giramabbhudīrayī,

Sīho yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito”ti. –

Having gone seven steps, Gotama looked upon the directions equally all around; he uttered a speech endowed with eight qualities, like a lion standing on a mountain peak.

Evaṃ tathā gatoti tathāgato.

Thus, because he has gone in such a way (tathā gato), he is the Tathāgata.

Atha [V 1.0052] vā yathā vipassī bhagavā…pe… yathā kassapo bhagavā, ayampi bhagavā tatheva nekkhammena kāmacchandaṃ pahāya gato. Abyāpādena byāpādaṃ, ālokasaññāya thinamiddhaṃ, avikkhepena uddhaccakukkuccaṃ, dhammavavatthānena vicikicchaṃ pahāya, ñāṇena avijjaṃ padāletvā, pāmojjena aratiṃ vinodetvā, paṭhamajjhānena nīvaraṇakavāṭaṃ ugghāṭetvā, dutiyajjhānena vitakkavicāradhūmaṃ vūpasametvā, tatiyajjhānena pītiṃ virājetvā, catutthajjhānena sukhadukkhaṃ pahāya, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā rūpasaññāpaṭighasaññānānattasaññāyo samatikkamitvā, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā ākāsānañcāyatanasaññaṃ, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā viññāṇañcāyatanasaññaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṃ samatikkamitvā gato.

Alternatively, just as the Blessed One Vipassī… and just as the Blessed One Kassapa, so too this Blessed One has gone in the very same way: having abandoned sensual desire through renunciation, he went. He went having abandoned ill will by non-ill will, sloth and torpor by the perception of light, restlessness and remorse by non-distraction, and doubt by the determination of phenomena. He went having shattered ignorance with knowledge, having dispelled discontent with joy, having opened the gate of the hindrances with the first jhāna, having stilled the smoke of thought and examination with the second jhāna, having become dispassionate towards rapture with the third jhāna, and having abandoned pleasure and pain with the fourth jhāna. He went having transcended perceptions of form, perceptions of resistance, and perceptions of diversity with the attainment of the base of infinite space; having transcended the perception of the base of infinite space with the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness; having transcended the perception of the base of infinite consciousness with the attainment of the base of nothingness; and having transcended the perception of the base of nothingness with the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Aniccānupassanāya niccasaññaṃ pahāya, dukkhānupassanāya sukhasaññaṃ, anattānupassanāya attasaññaṃ, nibbidānupassanāya nandiṃ, virāgānupassanāya rāgaṃ, nirodhānupassanāya samudayaṃ, paṭinissaggānupassanāya ādānaṃ, khayānupassanāya ghanasaññaṃ, vayānupassanāya āyūhanaṃ, vipariṇāmānupassanāya dhuvasaññaṃ, animittānupassanāya nimittaṃ, appaṇihitānupassanāya paṇidhiṃ, suññatānupassanāya abhinivesaṃ, adhipaññādhammavipassanāya sārādānābhinivesaṃ, yathābhūtañāṇadassanena sammohābhinivesaṃ, ādīnavānupassanāya ālayābhinivesaṃ, paṭisaṅkhānupassanāya appaṭisaṅkhaṃ, vivaṭṭānupassanāya saṃyogābhinivesaṃ, sotāpattimaggena diṭṭhekaṭṭhe kilese bhañjitvā, sakadāgāmimaggena oḷārike kilese pahāya, anāgāmimaggena aṇusahagate kilese samugghāṭetvā, arahattamaggena sabbakilese samucchinditvā gato. Evampi tathā gatoti tathāgato.

Having abandoned the perception of permanence by contemplating impermanence, the perception of happiness by contemplating suffering, the perception of self by contemplating non-self, delight by contemplating disenchantment, passion by contemplating dispassion, origination by contemplating cessation, grasping by contemplating relinquishment, the perception of compactness by contemplating destruction, accumulation by contemplating passing away, the perception of stability by contemplating change, the sign by contemplating the signless, aspiration by contemplating the desireless, adherence by contemplating emptiness, the adherence of grasping at a core by insight into phenomena with higher wisdom, adherence born of delusion by knowledge and vision of things as they truly are, adherence which is attachment by contemplating danger, non-reflection by contemplating reflective discernment, and adherence to the fetters by contemplating turning away; and having broken the defilements that share the same ground as wrong views by the path of stream-entry, having abandoned the gross defilements by the path of the once-returner, having uprooted the subtle defilements by the path of the non-returner, and having cut off all defilements without remainder by the path of Arahantship, he has gone. In this way also, because he has gone thus, he is the Tathāgata.

Kathaṃ [M 1.0050] tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgatoti tathāgato. Pathavīdhātuyā kakkhaḷattalakkhaṇaṃ tathaṃ avitathaṃ. Āpodhātuyā paggharaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Tejodhātuyā uṇhattalakkhaṇaṃ. Vāyodhātuyā vitthambhanalakkhaṇaṃ. Ākāsadhātuyā asamphuṭṭhalakkhaṇaṃ[P 1.0048]. Viññāṇadhātuyā vijānanalakkhaṇaṃ.

How is he the Tathāgata, as one who has come to the true characteristic? Of the earth element, the characteristic of hardness is true, not otherwise. Of the water element, the characteristic is flowing. Of the fire element, the characteristic is heat. Of the air element, the characteristic is supporting. Of the space element, the characteristic is being untouched. Of the consciousness element, the characteristic is cognizing.

Rūpassa ruppanalakkhaṇaṃ. Vedanāya vedayitalakkhaṇaṃ. Saññāya sañjānanalakkhaṇaṃ. Saṅkhārānaṃ abhisaṅkharaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Viññāṇassa vijānanalakkhaṇaṃ.

The characteristic of form is being afflicted. The characteristic of feeling is experiencing. The characteristic of perception is perceiving. The characteristic of volitional formations is fabricating. The characteristic of consciousness is cognizing.

Vitakkassa [V 1.0053] abhiniropanalakkhaṇaṃ. Vicārassa anumajjanalakkhaṇaṃ. Pītiyā pharaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Sukhassa sātalakkhaṇaṃ. Cittekaggatāya avikkhepalakkhaṇaṃ. Phassassa phusanalakkhaṇaṃ.

The characteristic of initial thought is directing onto an object. The characteristic of sustained thought is examining. The characteristic of rapture is suffusing. The characteristic of happiness is pleasantness. The characteristic of one-pointedness of mind is non-distraction. The characteristic of contact is touching.

Saddhindriyassa adhimokkhalakkhaṇaṃ. Vīriyindriyassa paggahaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Satindriyassa upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇaṃ. Samādhindriyassa avikkhepalakkhaṇaṃ. Paññindriyassa pajānanalakkhaṇaṃ.

The faculty of faith has the characteristic of conviction. The faculty of energy has the characteristic of exertion. The faculty of mindfulness has the characteristic of establishing. The faculty of concentration has the characteristic of non-distraction. The faculty of wisdom has the characteristic of understanding.

Saddhābalassa assaddhiye akampiyalakkhaṇaṃ. Vīriyabalassa kosajje. Satibalassa muṭṭhasacce. Samādhibalassa uddhacce. Paññābalassa avijjāya akampiyalakkhaṇaṃ.

The power of faith has the characteristic of being unshaken by faithlessness. The power of energy has the characteristic of being unshaken by laziness. The power of mindfulness has the characteristic of being unshaken by forgetfulness. The power of concentration has the characteristic of being unshaken by restlessness. The power of wisdom has the characteristic of being unshaken by ignorance.

Satisambojjhaṅgassa upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇaṃ. Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa pavicayalakkhaṇaṃ. Vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa paggahaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Pītisambojjhaṅgassa pharaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa upasamalakkhaṇaṃ. Samādhisambojjhaṅgassa avikkhepalakkhaṇaṃ. Upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa paṭisaṅkhānalakkhaṇaṃ.

The mindfulness awakening-factor has the characteristic of establishing. The investigation-of-phenomena awakening-factor has the characteristic of discerning. The energy awakening-factor has the characteristic of exertion. The rapture awakening-factor has the characteristic of suffusing. The tranquility awakening-factor has the characteristic of calming. The concentration awakening-factor has the characteristic of non-distraction. The equanimity awakening-factor has the characteristic of impartial observation.

Sammādiṭṭhiyā dassanalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammāsaṅkappassa abhiniropanalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammāvācāya pariggāhalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammākammantassa samuṭṭhānalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammāājīvassa vodānalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammāvāyāmassa paggahaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammāsatiyā upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammāsamādhissa avikkhepalakkhaṇaṃ.

Right view has the characteristic of seeing. Right thought has the characteristic of directing the mind. Right speech has the characteristic of encompassing. Right action has the characteristic of origination. Right livelihood has the characteristic of purification. Right effort has the characteristic of exertion. Right mindfulness has the characteristic of establishing. Right concentration has the characteristic of non-distraction.

Avijjāya aññāṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Saṅkhārānaṃ cetanālakkhaṇaṃ. Viññāṇassa vijānanalakkhaṇaṃ. Nāmassa namanalakkhaṇaṃ. Rūpassa ruppanalakkhaṇaṃ. Saḷāyatanassa āyatanalakkhaṇaṃ. Phassassa phusanalakkhaṇaṃ. Vedanāya vedayitalakkhaṇaṃ. Taṇhāya hetulakkhaṇaṃ. Upādānassa gahaṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Bhavassa āyūhanalakkhaṇaṃ. Jātiyā nibbattilakkhaṇaṃ. Jarāya jīraṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Maraṇassa cutilakkhaṇaṃ.

Ignorance has the characteristic of not knowing. Volitional formations have the characteristic of volition. Consciousness has the characteristic of cognizing. Name has the characteristic of inclining. Form has the characteristic of being afflicted. The six sense bases have the characteristic of being bases. Contact has the characteristic of touching. Feeling has the characteristic of experiencing. Craving has the characteristic of being a cause. Clinging has the characteristic of grasping. Becoming has the characteristic of striving. Birth has the characteristic of generation. Aging has the characteristic of decaying. Death has the characteristic of passing away.

Dhātūnaṃ [M 1.0051] suññatālakkhaṇaṃ. Āyatanānaṃ āyatanalakkhaṇaṃ. Satipaṭṭhānānaṃ upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇaṃ. Sammappadhānānaṃ padahanalakkhaṇaṃ. Iddhipādānaṃ ijjhanalakkhaṇaṃ. Indriyānaṃ adhipatilakkhaṇaṃ. Balānaṃ akampiyalakkhaṇaṃ. Bojjhaṅgānaṃ niyyānalakkhaṇaṃ. Maggassa hetulakkhaṇaṃ.

The elements have the characteristic of emptiness. The sense bases have the characteristic of being sense bases. The foundations of mindfulness have the characteristic of establishing. The right strivings have the characteristic of striving. The bases of spiritual power have the characteristic of accomplishment. The faculties have the characteristic of dominance. The powers have the characteristic of being unshakable. The factors of enlightenment have the characteristic of leading out. The path has the characteristic of being a cause.

Saccānaṃ [V 1.0054] tathalakkhaṇaṃ. Samathassa avikkhepalakkhaṇaṃ. Vipassanāya anupassanālakkhaṇaṃ. Samathavipassanānaṃ ekarasalakkhaṇaṃ. Yuganandhānaṃ [P 1.0049] anativattanalakkhaṇaṃ.

The truths have the characteristic of reality. Serenity has the characteristic of non-distraction. Insight has the characteristic of repeated contemplation. Serenity and insight have the characteristic of a single function. When yoked together, they have the characteristic of not overstepping one another.

Sīlavisuddhiyā saṃvaralakkhaṇaṃ. Cittavisuddhiyā avikkhepalakkhaṇaṃ. Diṭṭhivisuddhiyā dassanalakkhaṇaṃ.

Purification of virtue has the characteristic of restraint. Purification of mind has the characteristic of non-distraction. Purification of view has the characteristic of seeing.

Khayeñāṇassa samucchedalakkhaṇaṃ. Anuppāde ñāṇassa passaddhilakkhaṇaṃ. Chandassa mūlalakkhaṇaṃ. Manasikārassa samuṭṭhānalakkhaṇaṃ. Phassassa samodhānalakkhaṇaṃ. Vedanāya samosaraṇalakkhaṇaṃ. Samādhissa pamukhalakkhaṇaṃ. Satiyā ādhipateyyalakkhaṇaṃ. Paññāya tatuttarilakkhaṇaṃ. Vimuttiyā sāralakkhaṇaṃ. Amatogadhassa nibbānassa pariyosānalakkhaṇaṃ tathaṃ avitathaṃ. Evaṃ tathalakkhaṇaṃ ñāṇagatiyā āgato avirajjhitvā patto anuppattoti tathāgato, evaṃ tathalakkhaṇaṃ āgatoti tathāgato.

The knowledge of destruction has the characteristic of cutting off without remainder. The knowledge of non-arising has the characteristic of tranquility. Desire has the characteristic of being a root. Attention has the characteristic of origination. Contact has the characteristic of conjunction. Feeling has the characteristic of confluence. Concentration has the characteristic of being foremost. Mindfulness has the characteristic of dominance. Wisdom has the characteristic of being supreme thereto. Liberation has the characteristic of being the core. Nibbāna, which is the plunge into the deathless, has the characteristic of culmination—this is true, not otherwise. Thus, because he has come by the path of knowledge to the true characteristic, not deviating, having reached and attained it, he is the Tathāgata. Thus, because he has come to the true characteristic, he is the Tathāgata.

Kathaṃ tathadhamme yāthāvato abhisambuddhoti tathāgato? Tathadhammā nāma cattāri ariyasaccāni. Yathāha “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, tathāni avitathāni anaññathāni. Katamāni cattāri, idaṃ dukkhanti, bhikkhave, tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathameta”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.1050) vitthāro. Tāni ca bhagavā abhisambuddho, tasmā tathānaṃ abhisambuddhattā tathāgatoti vuccati. Abhisambuddhattho hi ettha gatasaddo. Apica jarāmaraṇassa jātipaccayasambhūtasamudāgataṭṭho tatho avitatho anaññatho…pe… saṅkhārānaṃ avijjāpaccayasambhūtasamudāgataṭṭho tatho avitatho anaññatho. Tathā avijjāya saṅkhārānaṃ paccayaṭṭho. Saṅkhārānaṃ viññāṇassa paccayaṭṭho…pe… jātiyā jarāmaraṇassa paccayaṭṭho tatho avitatho anaññatho. Taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavā abhisambuddho, tasmāpi tathānaṃ dhammānaṃ abhisambuddhattā tathāgatoti [M 1.0052] vuccati. Evaṃ tathadhamme yāthāvato abhisambuddhoti tathāgato.

How is it that because He has fully awakened to true phenomena as they really are, He is the Tathāgata? ‘True phenomena’ means the Four Noble Truths. As it is said: “Monks, these four are true, not unreal, not otherwise. What four? ‘This is suffering,’ monks, this is true, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise.” The detailed explanation should be known. And the Blessed One has fully awakened to those truths; therefore, because of having fully awakened to what is true, He is called the Tathāgata. For here, the word ‘gata’ has the meaning of ‘fully awakened.’ Furthermore, the characteristic of aging-and-death as having arisen and come into being from birth as its condition is true, not unreal, not otherwise… the characteristic of formations as having arisen and come into being from ignorance as its condition is true, not unreal, not otherwise. Likewise, the characteristic of ignorance as a condition for formations, the characteristic of formations as a condition for consciousness… the characteristic of birth as a condition for aging-and-death is true, not unreal, not otherwise. The Blessed One has fully awakened to all of that. Therefore, also because of having fully awakened to these true phenomena, He is called the Tathāgata. In this way, because He has fully awakened to true phenomena as they really are, He is the Tathāgata.

Kathaṃ tathadassitāya tathāgato? Bhagavā yaṃ sadevake loke…pe… sadevamanussāya aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu aparimāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ cakkhudvāre āpāthaṃ āgacchantaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ nāma atthi. Taṃ sabbākārato jānāti, passati. Evaṃ jānatā passatā ca tena taṃ iṭṭhāniṭṭhādivasena [V 1.0055] vā diṭṭhasutamutaviññātesu labbhamānakapadavasena vā “katamaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ, yaṃ rūpaṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ [P 1.0050] upādāya vaṇṇanibhā sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ nīlaṃ pītaka”nti (dha. sa. 616) ādinā nayena anekehi nāmehi terasahi vārehi dvepaññāsāya nayehi vibhajjamānaṃ tathameva hoti, vitathaṃ natthi. Esa nayo sotadvārādīsupi āpāthamāgacchantesu saddādīsu. Vuttañcetaṃ bhagavatā “yaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevakassa lokassa…pe… sadevamanussāya diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā, tamahaṃ jānāmi, …tamahaṃ abhiññāsiṃ, taṃ tathāgatassa viditaṃ, taṃ tathāgato na upaṭṭhāsī”ti (a. ni. 4.24). Evaṃ tathadassitāya tathāgato. Tattha tathadassīatthe tathāgatoti padasambhavo veditabbo.

How is it that because of seeing truly, He is the Tathāgata? Whatever visible object there is that comes into the range of the eye-door of countless beings in countless world-systems, in the world with its devas… with its devas and humans, the Blessed One knows and sees that object in all its aspects. By Him, thus knowing and seeing, that visible object—whether by way of the agreeable, disagreeable, and so on, or by way of the terms obtainable in what is seen, heard, sensed, and cognized—when analyzed by numerous names, thirteen sections, and fifty-two methods, in the manner beginning, “What is that form, the form-base, which, derived from the four great elements, is color, appearance, visible, and resistant, such as blue, yellow…”, is just so; it is not unreal. This same method should be understood for sounds and other objects that come into the range of the ear-door and so on. And this was stated by the Blessed One: “Monks, whatever in the world with its devas… with its devas and humans, is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and mentally traversed—that I know… that I have directly known. That is known to the Tathāgata, that is cognized by the Tathāgata, that has appeared to the Tathāgata.” In this way, because of seeing truly, He is the Tathāgata. Herein, the derivation of the word ‘Tathāgata’ should be understood in the sense of ‘one who sees thus’.

Kathaṃ tathāvāditāya tathāgato? Yaṃ rattiṃ bhagavā bodhimaṇḍe aparājitapallaṅke nisinno tiṇṇaṃ mārānaṃ matthakaṃ madditvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho, yañca rattiṃ yamakasālānamantare anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyi, etthantare pañcacattālīsavassaparimāṇe kāle paṭhamabodhiyāpi majjhimabodhiyāpi pacchimabodhiyāpi yaṃ bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ suttaṃ geyyaṃ…pe… vedallaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ atthato ca byañjanato ca anupavajjaṃ anūnamanadhikaṃ sabbākāraparipuṇṇaṃ rāgamadanimmadanaṃ dosamohamadanimmadanaṃ, natthi tattha vālaggamattampi pakkhalitaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ ekamuddikāya lañchitaṃ viya, ekanāḷiyā mitaṃ viya, ekatulāya tulitaṃ viya ca tathameva hoti avitathaṃ. Tenāha – “yañca, cunda, rattiṃ tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, yañca rattiṃ anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare bhāsati lapati niddisati, sabbaṃ taṃ tatheva hoti no aññathā. Tasmā tathāgatoti vuccatī”ti (a. ni. 4.23). Gadaattho [M 1.0053] hi ettha gatasaddo. Evaṃ tathāvāditāya tathāgato. Apica āgadanaṃ āgado, vacananti attho. Tatho aviparīto āgado assāti dakārassa takāraṃ katvā tathāgatoti evametasmiṃ atthe padasiddhi veditabbā.

How is it that because of speaking truly, He is the Tathāgata? On the night the Blessed One, seated on the unconquered throne at the Bodhi-maṇḍa, having crushed the heads of the three Māras, fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and on the night He attained parinibbāna in the Nibbāna-element without residue remaining between the twin sāla trees—whatever was spoken by the Blessed One in the interval of forty-five years, whether during the first, middle, or last period of His ministry, be it Sutta, Geyya… or Vedalla, all of it is faultless in both meaning and phrasing, not deficient, not excessive, complete in all aspects, the crusher of the intoxication of lust, the crusher of the intoxication of hatred and delusion. There is not even a hair’s tip of error therein. All of it is just so, not unreal, as if stamped with a single seal, as if measured with a single measure, as if weighed on a single balance. Therefore, He said: “Cunda, on the night the Tathāgata fully awakens to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and on the night He attains parinibbāna in the Nibbāna-element without residue remaining, whatever He speaks, utters, and declares in the interval, all of it is just so and not otherwise. Therefore, He is called the Tathāgata.” For here, the word ‘gata’ has the meaning of ‘spoken.’ In this way, because of speaking truly, He is the Tathāgata. Furthermore, ‘āgadanaṃ’ is ‘āgado,’ meaning ‘speech.’ ‘He has true, unperverted speech (tatho aviparīto āgado assā)’; thus, by changing the letter ‘d’ to ‘t,’ the word ‘Tathāgata’ is formed. The formation of the word in this sense should be understood in this way.

Kathaṃ [P 1.0051] tathākāritāya tathāgato? Bhagavato hi vācāya kāyo anulometi, kāyassapi vācā. Tasmā yathāvādī tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī ca hoti. Evaṃbhūtassa cassa yathā vācā[V 1.0056], kāyopi tathāgato pavattoti attho. Yathā ca kāyo, vācāpi tathā gatā pavattāti tathāgato. Tenāha “yathāvādī, bhikkhave, tathāgato tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī. Iti yathāvādī tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī, tasmā tathāgatoti vuccatī”ti (a. ni. 4.23). Evaṃ tathākāritāya tathāgato.

How is it that because of acting thus, He is the Tathāgata? Indeed, for the Blessed One, the body conforms to the speech, and the speech to the body. Therefore, as He speaks, so He acts; as He acts, so He speaks. And for one who is such, the meaning is: just as His speech proceeds, so (`tathā`) has His body gone (`gato`) or proceeded. And just as His body has proceeded, so (`tathā`) has His speech gone (`gatā`) or proceeded; hence, He is the Tathāgata. Therefore, He said: “Monks, as the Tathāgata speaks, so He acts; as He acts, so He speaks. Since as He speaks, so He acts, and as He acts, so He speaks, therefore He is called the Tathāgata.” In this way, because of acting thus, He is the Tathāgata.

Kathaṃ abhibhavanaṭṭhena tathāgato? Upari bhavaggaṃ heṭṭhā aviciṃ pariyantaṃ katvā tiriyaṃ aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu sabbasatte abhibhavati, sīlenapi samādhināpi paññāyapi vimuttiyāpi vimuttiñāṇadassanenapi, na tassa tulā vā pamāṇaṃ vā atthi, atulo appameyyo anuttaro rājarājo devadevo sakkānaṃ atisakko brahmānaṃ atibrahmā. Tenāha “sadevake, bhikkhave, loke…pe… sadevamanussāya tathāgato abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthu daso vasavattī. Tasmā tathāgatoti vuccatī”ti.

How is it that in the sense of overcoming, He is the Tathāgata? Having made the summit of existence the upper limit and Avīci the lower limit, He overcomes all beings in the immeasurable world-systems extending sideways—by virtue, by concentration, by wisdom, by liberation, and by the knowledge and vision of liberation. There is no equal or measure for Him; He is incomparable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, the King of kings, the Deva of devas, the Sakka beyond Sakkas, the Brahmā beyond Brahmās. Therefore, He said: “Monks, in the world with its devas… with its devas and humans, the Tathāgata is the overcomer, the unconquered, the all-seer, the master. Therefore, He is called the Tathāgata.”

Tatrevaṃ padasiddhi veditabbā, agado viya agado. Ko panesa? Desanāvilāsamayo ceva puññussayo ca. Tena hesa mahānubhāvo bhisakko dibbāgadena sappe viya sabbaparappavādino sadevakañca lokaṃ abhibhavati, iti sabbalokābhibhavane tatho aviparīto desanāvilāsamayo ceva puññassayo ca agado assāti dakārassa takāraṃ katvā tathāgatoti veditabbo. Evaṃ abhibhavanaṭṭhena tathāgato.

Herein, the formation of the word should be understood thus: Like an antidote, it is an antidote (`agado`). What is this? It is both the grace of the teaching and the proclamation of His glory. By this, this physician of great power overcomes all who hold other views and the world with its devas, just as one overcomes snakes with a divine antidote. Thus, because in overcoming the entire world He possesses an unfailing (`tatho`) antidote (`agado`)—which is the grace of the teaching and the proclamation of His glory—He should be known as `Tathāgata` by changing the letter 'd' to 't'. Thus, He is the Tathāgata in the sense of overcoming.

Apica tathāya gatotipi tathāgato, tathaṃ gatotipi tathāgato. Gatoti avagato, atīto, patto, paṭipannoti attho. Tattha [M 1.0054] sakalaṃ lokaṃ tīraṇapariññāya tathāya gato avagatoti tathāgato. Lokasamudayaṃ pahānapariññāya tathāya gato atītoti tathāgato. Lokanirodhaṃ sacchikiriyāya tathāya gato pattoti tathāgato. Lokanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ tathaṃ gato paṭipannoti tathāgato. Tena yaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā “loko, bhikkhave, tathāgatena abhisambuddho, lokasmā tathāgato visaṃyutto. Lokasamudayo, bhikkhave, tathāgatena abhisambuddho, lokasamudayo tathāgatassa [P 1.0052] pahīno. Lokanirodho, bhikkhave, tathāgatena abhisambuddho, lokanirodho tathāgatassa sacchikato. Lokanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, bhikkhave, tathāgatena abhisambuddhā, lokanirodhagāminī paṭipadā tathāgatassa bhāvitā. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevakassa [V 1.0057] lokassa…pe… sabbaṃ taṃ tathāgatena abhisambuddhaṃ, tasmā tathāgatoti vuccatī”ti (a. ni. 4.23). Tassa evampi attho veditabbo. Idampi ca tathāgatassa tathāgatabhāvadīpane mukhamattameva. Sabbākārena pana tathāgatova tathāgatassa tathāgatabhāvaṃ vaṇṇeyya.

Alternatively, He is the Tathāgata because He has gone undeviatingly (`tathāya gato`); He is the Tathāgata because He has gone to the truth (`tathaṃ gato`). Here, 'gone' (`gato`) has the meaning of known (`avagato`), overcome (`atīto`), reached (`patto`), and practiced (`paṭipanno`). Therein, He is the Tathāgata because He has known the entire world through the undeviating comprehension by determining. He is the Tathāgata because He has overcome the origin of the world through the undeviating comprehension by abandoning. He is the Tathāgata because He has reached the cessation of the world through undeviating realization. He is the Tathāgata because He has practiced the true path leading to the cessation of the world. Therefore, it was said by the Blessed One: 'Bhikkhus, the world has been fully awakened to by the Tathāgata; the Tathāgata is detached from the world. The origin of the world, bhikkhus, has been fully awakened to by the Tathāgata; the origin of the world has been abandoned by the Tathāgata. The cessation of the world, bhikkhus, has been fully awakened to by the Tathāgata; the cessation of the world has been realized by the Tathāgata. The path leading to the cessation of the world, bhikkhus, has been fully awakened to by the Tathāgata; the path leading to the cessation of the world has been developed by the Tathāgata. Whatever, bhikkhus, in the world with its devas… all that has been fully awakened to by the Tathāgata. Therefore, He is called the Tathāgata.' The meaning of the term should also be understood in this way. And this, in explaining the state of a Tathāgata, is merely a foretaste. For in all aspects, only a Tathāgata could describe the Tathāgata-nature of a Tathāgata.

Arahaṃ sammāsambuddhoti padadvaye pana ārakattā arīnaṃ, arānañca hatattā, paccayādīnaṃ arahattā, pāpakaraṇe rahābhāvāti imehi tāva kāraṇehi arahanti veditabbo.

Now, in the pair of terms `Arahaṃ Sammāsambuddho`, He should be known as `Arahaṃ` for these reasons: because of His farness (from defilements), because He has slain the enemies (the defilements), because He has destroyed the spokes (of the wheel of saṃsāra), because He is worthy (of requisites and so on), and because He has no secret place for doing evil.

Sammā sāmañca sabbadhammānaṃ buddhattā pana sammāsambuddhoti. Ayamettha saṅkhepo. Vitthārato panetaṃ padadvayaṃ visuddhimagge buddhānussativaṇṇanāyaṃ pakāsitaṃ.

He is the `Sammāsambuddha` (Perfectly Self-Enlightened One) because He has rightly and by Himself understood all things. This is the summary here. In detail, however, this pair of terms is explained in the Visuddhimagga in the exposition on the Recollection of the Buddha.

Pariññātantaṃ tathāgatassāti ettha pana taṃ maññanāvatthu pariññātaṃ tathāgatassātipi attho veditabbo. Pariññātantaṃ nāma pariññātapāraṃ pariññātāvasānaṃ anavasesato pariññātanti vuttaṃ hoti. Buddhānañhi sāvakehi saddhiṃ kiñcāpi tena tena maggena kilesappahāne viseso natthi, pariññāya pana atthi. Sāvakā hi catunnaṃ dhātūnaṃ ekadesameva sammasitvā nibbānaṃ pāpuṇanti. Buddhānaṃ pana aṇuppamāṇampi saṅkhāragataṃ ñāṇena adiṭṭhamatulitamatīritamasacchikataṃ natthi.

“That has been fully comprehended by the Tathāgata.” Herein, the meaning should also be understood as: “That object of conceiving has been fully comprehended by the Tathāgata.” The term “fully comprehended to the end” (pariññātantaṃ) means that it is said to be comprehended to the perfection of full comprehension, to the conclusion of full comprehension, comprehended without remainder. For although there is no difference between Buddhas and their disciples in the abandoning of defilements by means of this or that path, there is a difference in full comprehension. Indeed, disciples reach Nibbāna by contemplating only a portion of the four elements. But for the Buddhas, there is not even an infinitesimal amount among conditioned things that has not been seen, not weighed, not judged, and not realized by Their knowledge.

Tathāgatavārasattamanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the seventh method in the section on the Tathāgata is concluded.

Tathāgatavāraaṭṭhamanayavaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Eighth Method in the Section on the Tathāgata
