Tassattho – yvāyaṃ anāgāmī bhikkhu evaṃ “buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti…pe… dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā”ti, tassa yathodhi kho cattaṃ hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, sakasakaodhivasena cattameva hoti, taṃ taṃ kilesajātaṃ vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ. Sakasakaodhivasenāti dve odhī kilesodhi ca maggodhi ca. Tattha kilesodhivasenāpi ye kilesā yaṃ maggavajjhā, te aññamaggavajjhehi amissā hutvā sakeneva odhinā pahīnā. Maggodhivasenāpi ye kilesā yena maggena pahātabbā, tena teyeva pahīnā [V 1.0182] honti. Evaṃ sakasakaodhivasena taṃ taṃ kilesajātaṃ cattameva hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, taṃ paccavekkhitvā ca laddhasomanasso tatuttaripi so “buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī”ti labhati atthavedanti sambandho.

This is its meaning: For that non-returning bhikkhu who is thus 'endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha… the Dhamma… the Saṅgha… the unsurpassed field of merit for the world,' for him, according to the boundary, it is abandoned, it is relinquished. By means of one's own respective boundary, it is indeed abandoned; that particular kind of defilement is vomited, released, given up, and relinquished. 'By means of one's own respective boundary' refers to two boundaries: the boundary of defilements and the boundary of the path. Therein, by way of the boundary of defilements, those defilements that are to be destroyed by a particular path are abandoned by their own boundary, unmixed with defilements to be destroyed by another path. And by way of the boundary of the path, those defilements that are to be abandoned by a particular path are abandoned by that very path. Thus, by means of one's own respective boundary, that particular kind of defilement is indeed abandoned and relinquished. And having reviewed that and obtained gladness, he, even further, obtains the joy related to the meaning, thinking, 'I am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha.' Thus is the connection to be understood.

Yatodhi [P 1.0173] khotipi pāṭho. Tassa vasena ayamattho, assa bhikkhuno yatodhi kho pana cattaṃ hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ. Tattha yatoti kāraṇavacanaṃ, yasmāti vuttaṃ hoti. Odhīti heṭṭhā tayo maggā vuccanti. Kasmā? Te hi odhiṃ katvā koṭṭhāsaṃ katvā uparimaggena pahātabbakilese ṭhapetvā pajahanti, tasmā odhīti vuccanti. Arahattamaggo pana kiñci kilesaṃ anavasesetvā pajahati, tasmā anodhīti vuccati. Imassa ca bhikkhuno heṭṭhāmaggattayena cattaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “yatodhi kho panassa cattaṃ hotī”ti. Tattha kho panāti nipātamattaṃ. Ayaṃ pana piṇḍattho. Yasmā assa odhi cattaṃ hoti paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ, tasmā taṃ paccavekkhitvā ca laddhasomanasso tatuttaripi so “buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatomhī”ti labhati atthavedanti yathāpāḷi netabbaṃ.

There is also the reading 'yatodhi kho.' According to that, this is the meaning: for this bhikkhu, because it is abandoned and relinquished with a boundary. Therein, 'yato' is a causal term; it means 'yasmā' (because). By 'odhi' (boundary), the three lower paths are meant. Why? Because they, having made a boundary, having made a portion, abandon defilements while setting aside those to be abandoned by the higher path. Therefore, they are called 'odhi' (with a boundary). The path of Arahantship, however, abandons every single defilement without remainder; therefore, it is called 'anodhi' (without a boundary). And for this bhikkhu, defilements are abandoned by the three lower paths. Therefore it was said, 'Because for him it is abandoned with a boundary.' Herein, 'kho pana' are mere particles. This, however, is the summary meaning: Because for him it is abandoned and relinquished with a boundary, therefore, having reviewed that and obtained gladness, he, even further, obtains the joy related to the meaning, thinking, 'I am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha.' Thus it should be construed in accordance with the Pāli.

Tattha cattanti idaṃ sakabhāvapariccajanavasena vuttaṃ. Vantanti idaṃ pana anādiyanabhāvadassanavasena. Muttanti idaṃ santatito vinimocanavasena. Pahīnanti idaṃ muttassapi kvaci anavaṭṭhānadassanavasena. Paṭinissaṭṭhanti idaṃ pubbe ādinnapubbassa [M 1.0178] paṭinissaggadassanavasena paṭimukhaṃ vā nissaṭṭhabhāvadassanavasena bhāvanābalena abhibhuyya nissaṭṭhabhāvadassanavasenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Labhati atthavedaṃ labhati dhammavedanti ettha buddhādīsu aveccappasādoyeva araṇīyato attho, upagantabbatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Dhāraṇato dhammo, vinipatituṃ appadānatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Vedoti ganthopi ñāṇampi somanassampi. “Tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū”tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.256) hi gantho “vedo”ti vuccati. “Yaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vedagumābhijaññā, akiñcanaṃ kāmabhāve asatta”ntiādīsu (su. ni. 1065) ñāṇaṃ. “Ye vedajātā vicaranti loke”tiādīsu somanassaṃ. Idha pana somanassañca somanassasampayuttañāṇañca adhippetaṃ, tasmā “labhati atthavedaṃ labhati dhammavedanti aveccappasādārammaṇasomanassañca somanassamayañāṇañca labhatī”ti evamettha attho veditabbo.

Therein, this word 'abandoned' (catta) is spoken by way of forsaking one's own state. This word 'vomited' (vanta) is by way of showing the state of not taking up again. This word 'released' (mutta) is by way of complete release from the continuity. This word 'given up' (pahīna) is by way of showing non-establishment anywhere even for one who is released. This word 'relinquished' (paṭinissaṭṭha) is said to be by way of showing the relinquishment of what was formerly grasped; or by way of showing the state of being relinquished face-to-face; or by way of showing the state of being relinquished by having subdued it through the power of mental development. In the phrase 'He obtains the joy of the meaning, he obtains the joy of the Dhamma,' 'meaning' (attha) refers to unwavering confidence in the Buddha and so on, because it is to be resorted to; that is to say, it is to be approached. 'Dhamma' is so called because it upholds, because it does not allow one to fall into ruin. 'Veda' can mean scripture, knowledge, or gladness. Indeed, in passages such as 'gone to the far shore of the three Vedas,' 'veda' refers to scripture. In passages such as 'That Brahmin you should know as a master of vedas, having nothing, unattached to the realm of sensual pleasures,' it refers to knowledge. In passages such as 'Those who, born of joy, wander in the world,' it refers to gladness. Here, however, both gladness and the knowledge associated with gladness are intended. Therefore, the meaning here in 'He obtains the joy of the meaning, he obtains the joy of the Dhamma' should be understood thus: 'He obtains the gladness that has unwavering confidence as its object, and the knowledge that is accompanied by gladness.'

Atha [V 1.0183] vā atthavedanti aveccappasādaṃ paccavekkhato uppannaṃ vuttappakārameva vedaṃ. Dhammavedanti [P 1.0174] aveccappasādassa hetuṃ odhiso kilesappahānaṃ paccavekkhato uppannaṃ vuttappakārameva vedanti evampi ettha attho veditabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ “hetumhi ñāṇaṃ dhammapaṭisambhidā, hetuphale ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā”ti (vibha. 718-719). Dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjanti tameva atthañca dhammañca atthadhammānisaṃsabhūtaṃ vedañca paccavekkhato uppannaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Tañhi anavajjalakkhaṇena paccavekkhaṇākārappavattena dhammena upasañhitanti vuccati. Pamuditassa pīti jāyatīti iminā pāmojjena pamuditassa nirāmisā pīti jāyati. Pītimanassāti tāya pītiyā pīṇitamanassa. Kāyo passambhatīti kāyopi passaddho hoti vūpasantadaratho. Passaddhakāyo sukhanti evaṃ vūpasantakāyadaratho cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Cittaṃ samādhiyatīti cittaṃ sammā ādhiyati appitaṃ viya acalaṃ tiṭṭhati.

Alternatively, 'joy in the meaning' is the aforementioned joy that arises for one who reflects on unwavering faith. 'Joy in the Dhamma' is the aforementioned joy that arises for one who reflects on the abandonment of defilements by delimitation, which is the cause of unwavering faith. Thus, the meaning should be understood here in this way as well. For it has been said: “Knowledge in the cause is the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma; knowledge in the result of the cause is the analytical knowledge of the meaning.” 'Joy connected with the Dhamma' is the joy that arises for one who reflects on that very meaning and Dhamma, and on the joy that is the benefit of that meaning and Dhamma. For it is called 'connected with the Dhamma' because it is connected with the Dhamma, which has the characteristic of blamelessness and proceeds by way of reflection. 'For one who is joyful, rapture arises' means that for one who is gladdened by this joy, non-sensual rapture arises. 'With a rapturous mind' means for one whose mind is gladdened by that rapture. 'The body becomes tranquil' means the body also becomes calm, its distress having ceased. 'One with a tranquil body feels happiness' means that one whose bodily distress has thus ceased experiences mental happiness. 'The mind becomes concentrated' means the mind is well established; it stands unmoving, as if fixed.

76. Evamassa kilesappahānaṃ aveccappasādasamannāgataṃ paccavekkhato uppajjamānaṃ somanassādiānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā idāni “yathodhi kho pana me”ti vārena tassa paccavekkhaṇāya pavattākāraṃ pakāsetvā tasseva [M 1.0179] anāgāmimaggānubhāvasūcakaṃ phalaṃ dassento sa kho so, bhikkhavetiādimāha.

76. Thus, having shown the benefits of joy and so forth that arise for him when he reflects on the abandonment of defilements, which is endowed with unwavering faith, now, by means of the passage 'Insofar as for me...', he reveals the manner in which that reflection occurs, and then, showing the fruit that indicates the power of the non-returner's path, he says the words beginning, 'That, bhikkhus, is...'

Tattha evaṃsīloti tassa anāgāmimaggasampayuttaṃ sīlakkhandhaṃ dasseti. Evaṃdhammo evaṃpaññoti taṃsampayuttameva samādhikkhandhaṃ paññākkhandhañca dasseti. Sālīnanti lohitasāligandhasāliādīnaṃ anekarūpānaṃ. Piṇḍapātanti odanaṃ. Vicitakāḷakanti apanītakāḷakaṃ. Nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāyāti tassa evaṃvidhassa bhikkhuno taṃ vuttappakārapiṇḍapātabhojanaṃ maggassa vā phalassa vā neva antarāyāya hoti, paṭiladdhaguṇassa hi taṃ kimantarāyaṃ karissati? Yopissa appaṭiladdho catutthamaggo ca phalaṃ ca tappaṭilābhāya vipassanaṃ ārabhatopi nevassa taṃ hoti antarāyāya, antarāyaṃ kātuṃ asamatthameva hoti. Kasmā? Vuttappakārasīladhammapaññāsaṅgahena maggena visuddhacittattā.

Here, 'thus virtuous' indicates the virtue aggregate associated with the path of the non-returner. 'Thus endowed with Dhamma, thus wise' indicates the concentration aggregate and the wisdom aggregate associated with it. 'Fine rice' refers to various kinds such as red rice, fragrant rice, and so on. 'Almsfood' means cooked rice. 'Free from dark grains' means with the black grains removed. 'Nor is that an obstacle for him'—for a bhikkhu of such a kind, that almsfood of the described sort is no obstacle to the path or the fruit. For one who has attained the qualities, what obstacle could it cause? Even if he has not yet attained the fourth path and its fruit, and he begins insight meditation for their attainment, still that is no obstacle for him; it is simply incapable of causing an obstacle. Why? Because his mind is purified by the path, which is encompassed by virtue, Dhamma, and wisdom as described.

Yasmā [P 1.0175] cettha etadeva kāraṇaṃ, tasmā tadanurūpaṃ upamaṃ dassento seyyathāpītiādimāha.

Since this is the reason here, therefore, to illustrate accordingly, he says, 'Just as...'

Tattha [V 1.0184] acchanti vippasannaṃ. Parisuddhaṃ malavigamena. Pariyodātaṃ pabhassaratāya. Ukkāmukhanti suvaṇṇakārānaṃ mūsāmukhaṃ. Suvaṇṇakārānaṃ mūsā hi idha ukkā, aññattha pana dīpikādayopi vuccanti. “Ukkāsu dhārīyamānāsū”ti (dī. ni. 1.159) hi āgataṭṭhāne dīpikā “ukkā”ti vuccati. “Ukkaṃ bandheyya, ukkaṃ bandhitvā ukkāmukhaṃ ālimpeyyā”ti (ma. ni. 3.360) āgataṭṭhāne aṅgārakapallaṃ. “Kammārānaṃ yathā ukkā, anto jhāyati no bahī”ti (jā. 2.22.649) āgataṭṭhāne kammāruddhanaṃ. “Evaṃvipāko ukkāpāto bhavissatī”ti (dī. ni. 1.24) āgataṭṭhāne vātavego “ukkā”ti vuccati. Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne aññesu ca evarūpesu “saṇḍāsena jātarūpaṃ gahetvā ukkāmukhe pakkhipatī”ti āgataṭṭhānesu suvaṇṇakārānaṃ mūsā “ukkā”ti veditabbā.

Herein, accha means very clear. Parisuddha means pure by the removal of impurities. Pariyodāta means spotless by its radiance. Ukkāmukha means the mouth of a goldsmith's crucible. For here, the goldsmith's crucible is called ukkā, but elsewhere, torches and so on are also called by this term. For in the passage where it says, “when torches are being carried” (DN 1.159), a torch is called ukkā. In the passage where it says, “one should bind a charcoal pan, and having bound the charcoal pan, one should smear its mouth” (MN 3.360), it refers to a charcoal pan. In the passage where it says, “like the ukkā of smiths, it burns inside, not outside” (Ja 2.22.649), it refers to a smith's bellows. In the passage where it says, “such will be the result, a meteor-fall” (DN 1.24), a gust of wind is called ukkā. But in this passage and in other similar instances—such as in the passage “taking gold with tongs and placing it in the mouth of the ukkā”—the goldsmith's crucible should be understood as the ukkā.

Tatrāyaṃ upamāsaṃsandanā – saṃkiliṭṭhavatthaṃ viya hi saṃkiliṭṭhajātarūpaṃ viya ca imassa bhikkhuno puthujjanakāle kāmarāgādimalānugataṃ cittaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Acchodakaṃ viya ukkāmukhaṃ viya ca anāgāmimaggo. Taṃ udakaṃ ukkāmukhañca [M 1.0180] āgamma vatthasuvaṇṇānaṃ parisuddhatā viya tassa bhikkhuno vuttappakārasīladhammapaññāsaṅgahaṃ anāgāmimaggaṃ āgamma visuddhacittatāti.

Herein is the correlation of the simile: The mind of this bhikkhu in his time as a worldling, followed by defilements such as sensual desire, should be seen as being like a soiled cloth and like impure gold. The path of the non-returner should be seen as being like clear water and like a crucible-mouth. Just as the purity of the cloth and gold is achieved by means of that water and that crucible-mouth, so too the purity of mind of that bhikkhu is achieved by means of the non-returner's path, which is comprised of virtue, concentration, and wisdom of the kind already mentioned.

77. So mettāsahagatena cetasāti yathānusandhivasena desanā āgatā. Tayo hi anusandhī pucchānusandhi ajjhāsayānusandhi yathānusandhīti. Tattha “evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca ‘siyā nu kho, bhante, bahiddhā asati paritassanā’ti? ‘Siyā bhikkhū’ti bhagavā avocā”ti (ma. ni. 1.242). Evaṃ pucchantānaṃ vissajjitasuttavasena pucchānusandhi veditabbo. “Siyā kho pana te brāhmaṇa evamassa, ajjāpi nūna samaṇo gotamo avītarāgo”ti (ma. ni. 1.55) evaṃ paresaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā vuttassa suttassa vasena ajjhāsayānusandhi veditabbo. Yena pana dhammena ādimhi desanā uṭṭhitā, tassa dhammassa anurūpadhammavasena vā paṭipakkhavasena vā yesu suttesu upari desanā āgacchati, tesaṃ vasena yathānusandhi veditabbo[P 1.0176]. Seyyathidaṃ, ākaṅkheyyasutte heṭṭhā sīlena desanā uṭṭhitā, upari cha abhiññā āgatā. Kakacūpame heṭṭhā akkhantiyā uṭṭhitā, upari kakacūpamovādo āgato. Alagadde heṭṭhā diṭṭhiparidīpanena uṭṭhitā, upari tiparivaṭṭasuññatāpakāsanā āgatā, cūḷaassapure heṭṭhā kilesaparidīpanena uṭṭhitā, upari brahmavihārā [V 1.0185] āgatā. Kosambiyasutte heṭṭhā bhaṇḍanena uṭṭhitā, upari sāraṇīyadhammā āgatā. Imasmimpi vatthasutte heṭṭhā kilesaparidīpanena uṭṭhitā, upari brahmavihārā āgatā. Tena vuttaṃ “yathānusandhivasena desanā āgatā”ti. Brahmavihāresu pana anupadavaṇṇanā ca bhāvanānayo ca sabbo sabbākārena visuddhimagge vutto.

77. Regarding the phrase 'He with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness,' the teaching has proceeded by way of natural correspondence. Indeed, there are three connections: the connection of questioning, the connection of underlying disposition, and the connection of natural correspondence. Among these, the connection of questioning should be understood by way of suttas that are given in answer to those who ask, such as: “When this was said, a certain monk said to the Blessed One, ‘Venerable sir, might there be non-agitation regarding external things?’ ‘There might be, monk,’ the Blessed One replied.” The connection of underlying disposition should be understood by way of a sutta that is taught after knowing the disposition of others, such as: “Brahmin, it might occur to you, ‘Even today, the ascetic Gotama is not free from lust.’” The connection of natural correspondence should be understood by way of those suttas where the teaching arises at the beginning with a certain principle, and the teaching that comes later proceeds either in accordance with that principle or in opposition to it. For instance: In the Ākaṅkheyya Sutta, the teaching arises at the beginning with virtue, and later the six higher knowledges are introduced. In the Kakacūpama Sutta, the teaching arises at the beginning with non-tolerance, and later the exhortation of the simile of the saw is introduced. In the Alagaddūpama Sutta, the teaching arises at the beginning with the exposition of views, and later the explanation of the emptiness of the three rounds is introduced. In the Cūḷa-Assapura Sutta, the teaching arises at the beginning with the exposition of defilements, and later the divine abodes are introduced. In the Kosambiya Sutta, the teaching arises at the beginning with quarreling, and later the principles of cordiality are introduced. In this very Vatthasutta (Discourse on the Cloth) as well, the teaching arises at the beginning with the exposition of defilements, and later the divine abodes are introduced. Therefore, it was said, “the teaching has proceeded by way of natural correspondence.” As for the divine abodes, the sequential word-explanation and the method of cultivation are all stated in every way in the Visuddhimagga.

78. Evaṃ bhagavā abhijjhādīnaṃ upakkilesānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtaṃ sabbaso ca kāmarāgabyāpādappahānena vihatapaccatthikattā laddhapadaṭṭhānaṃ tassa anāgāmino brahmavihārabhāvanaṃ dassetvā idānissa arahattāya vipassanaṃ dassetvā arahattappattiṃ dassetuṃ so atthi idantiādimāha.

78. Thus the Blessed One, having shown to that non-returner the cultivation of the divine abodes—which is the counterpart to the defilements of covetousness and so on, and which has its basis established due to the destruction of adversaries through the complete abandonment of sensual lust and ill will—now, in order to show the attainment of Arahantship by showing insight for the sake of his Arahantship, spoke the words beginning with, "He... 'There is this...'"

Tassattho – so anāgāmī evaṃ bhāvitabrahmavihāro etesaṃ brahmavihārānaṃ yato kutoci vuṭṭhāya te eva brahmavihāradhamme nāmavasena [M 1.0181] tesaṃ nissayaṃ hadayavatthuṃ vatthunissayāni bhūtānīti iminā nayena bhūtupādāyadhamme rūpavasena ca vavatthapetvā atthi idanti pajānāti, ettāvatānena dukkhasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tato tassa dukkhassa samudayaṃ paṭivijjhanto atthi hīnanti pajānāti, ettāvatānena samudayasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tato tassa pahānupāyaṃ vicinanto atthi paṇītanti pajānāti, ettāvatānena maggasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tato tena maggena adhigantabbaṭṭhānaṃ vicinanto atthi uttari imassa saññāgatassa nissaraṇanti pajānāti, imassa mayā adhigatassa brahmavihārasaññāgatassa uttari nissaraṇaṃ nibbānaṃ atthīti evaṃ pajānātīti adhippāyo, ettāvatānena nirodhasaccavavatthānaṃ kataṃ hoti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passatoti tassa vipassanāpaññāya evaṃ catūhi [P 1.0177] ākārehi cattāri saccāni jānato, maggapaññāya evaṃ passato, bhayabherave vuttanayeneva kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati…pe… itthattāyāti pajānātīti.

Its meaning is this: That non-returner, having thus cultivated the divine abodes, arises from any one of these divine abodes and determines those very divine abode states by way of name. Then, having determined their support—the heart-basis—and the primary elements which support that basis, in this way determining by way of materiality the material phenomena based on the primary elements, he understands, "This exists." To this extent, the determination of the truth of suffering has been accomplished by him. Thereafter, penetrating the origin of that suffering, he understands, "The inferior exists." To this extent, the determination of the truth of the origin has been accomplished by him. Thereafter, investigating the means for its abandonment, he understands, "The excellent exists." To this extent, the determination of the truth of the path has been accomplished by him. Thereafter, investigating the state to be reached by that path, he understands, "There is a further escape from this which has been reached through perception." The intended meaning is that he understands thus: "There is Nibbāna, the escape beyond this object of divine-abode-perception that I have attained." To this extent, the determination of the truth of cessation has been accomplished by him. For him, thus knowing and thus seeing—that is, for him knowing the four truths in four aspects with insight wisdom and seeing them thus with path wisdom—his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, just as was stated in the Bhayabherava Sutta... and so on... he understands: "there is no more for this state of being."

Evaṃ yāva arahattā desanaṃ pāpetvā idāni yasmā tassaṃ parisati nhānasuddhiko brāhmaṇo nisinno, so evaṃ nhānasuddhiyā vaṇṇaṃ vuccamānaṃ sutvā pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissatīti bhagavatā vidito, tasmā tassa codanatthāya “ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [V 1.0186] sināto antarena sinānenā”ti imaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ anusandhimāha. Tattha antarena sinānenāti abbhantarena kilesavuṭṭhānasinānena.

Thus, having brought the teaching up to Arahantship, now, because a brahmin who held the view of purification by bathing was seated in that assembly—and it was known by the Blessed One that this brahmin, upon hearing the praise of purification by bathing, would go forth and attain Arahantship—therefore, for the purpose of prompting him, He spoke this specific connection: “This, monks, is called a monk who is bathed with an inner bathing.” Therein, “with an inner bathing” means with the inner bathing that is the cleansing of the stain of defilements.

79. Sundarikabhāradvājoti bhāradvājo nāma so brāhmaṇo attano gottavasena, sundarikāya pana nadiyā sinātassa pāpappahānaṃ hotīti ayamassa diṭṭhi, tasmā “sundarikabhāradvājo”ti vuccati. So taṃ bhagavato vacanaṃ sutvā cintesi “mayaṃ sinānasuddhiṃ vaṇṇema, samaṇopi gotamo tatheva vaṇṇeti, samānacchando dāni esa amhehī”ti. Atha bhagavantaṃ bāhukaṃ nadiṃ gantvā taṃ tattha pāpaṃ pavāhetvā āgataṃ viya maññamāno āha “gacchati pana bhavaṃ gotamo bāhukaṃ nadiṃ sināyitu”nti? Bhagavā tassa gacchāmīti vā na gacchāmīti vā avatvāyeva brāhmaṇassa diṭṭhisamugghātaṃ kattukāmo “kiṃ brāhmaṇa bāhukāya nadiyā[M 1.0182], kiṃ bāhukā nadī karissatī”ti āha. Tassattho kiṃ payojanaṃ bāhukāya, kiṃ sā karissati? Asamatthā sā kassaci atthāya, kiṃ tattha gamissāmīti?

79. Regarding "Sundarikabhāradvāja": That brahmin was named Bhāradvāja on account of his clan. However, because he held the wrong view that "for one who has bathed in the Sundarikā river, there is an abandoning of evil," he is called "Sundarikabhāradvāja." Having heard that statement from the Blessed One, he thought: "We too praise purification by bathing, and the ascetic Gotama also praises it in the same way. Now he is of the same inclination as us." Then, thinking of the Blessed One as one who had gone to the Bāhukā river to wash away his evil there and returned, he asked, "Does the honorable Gotama go to the Bāhukā river to bathe?" The Blessed One, without saying either "I go" or "I do not go," wishing to eradicate the brahmin's wrong view, said, "What, brahmin, of the Bāhukā river? What will the Bāhukā river do?" Its meaning is: What is the use of the Bāhukā? What can it do? It is incapable of bringing about benefit for anyone, so why should I go there?

Atha brāhmaṇo taṃ pasaṃsanto lokkhasammatātiādimāha. Tattha lokkhasammatāti lūkhabhāvasammatā, lūkhabhāvanti cokkhabhāvaṃ, visuddhibhāvaṃ detīti evaṃ sammatāti vuttaṃ hoti. Lokyasammatātipi pāṭho. Tassattho, seṭṭhaṃ lokaṃ gamayatīti evaṃ sammatāti. Puññasammatāti puññanti sammatā. Pavāhetīti gamayati visodheti. Gāthāhi ajjhabhāsīti gāthāhi abhāsi. Gāthā ca vuccamānā tadatthadīpanatthameva vā gāthārucikānaṃ vuccati, visesatthadīpanatthaṃ vā. Idha panetā ubhayatthadīpanatthaṃ vuttāti [P 1.0178] veditabbā.

Then the brahmin, wishing to praise that river, spoke the words beginning with 'Lokkhasammatā.' Therein, 'Lokkhasammatā' means designated as giving a state of purity; 'lūkhabhāvaṃ' means the state of being pure, the state of being cleansed; 'it gives'—thus it is designated. This is what is meant. There is also the reading 'Lokyasammatā.' Its meaning is: it is designated as that which leads to a noble world. 'Puññasammatā' means designated as merit. 'Pavāheti' means it conveys, it purifies. 'He spoke in verses' (gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi) means he spoke in verses. And verses, when spoken, are spoken either just to explain the meaning of the preceding teaching for those who delight in verses, or to explain a special meaning. But here, it should be known that these verses are spoken to explain both purposes.

Bāhukanti idameva hi ettha vacanaṃ tadatthadīpakaṃ, sesāni visesatthadīpakāni. Yatheva hi bāhukaṃ, evaṃ adhikakkādīnipi loko gacchati nhānena pāpaṃ pavāhetuṃ. Tattha ye tesaṃ ṭhānānaṃ āsannā honti, te divasassa tikkhattuṃ nhāyanti. Ye dūrā, te yathākkamaṃ dvikkhattuṃ sakiṃ ekadivasantaraṃ, evaṃ yāva saṃvaccharantaraṃ nhāyanti. Ye pana sabbathāpi gantuṃ na sakkonti, te ghaṭehipi tato udakaṃ āharāpetvā nhāyanti. Sabbañcetaṃ niratthakaṃ, tasmā imaṃ visesatthaṃ dīpetuṃ adhikakkādīnipīti āha.

Indeed, here only this word 'Bāhukaṃ' explains that meaning, while the remaining words explain the special meanings. Indeed, just as the populace goes to the Bāhukā to wash away evil by bathing, so too the populace goes to the Adhikakka and other fords to wash away evil by bathing. Among them, those who are near those places bathe three times a day. Those who are far bathe, respectively, twice, once, every other day, and so on, up to once a year. But those who are altogether unable to go, they have water brought from there in pots and bathe. And all this is fruitless. Therefore, to explain this special meaning, he said, 'Adhikakkādīni hi.'

Tattha [V 1.0187] adhikakkanti nhānasambhāravasena laddhavohāraṃ ekaṃ titthaṃ vuccati. Gayātipi maṇḍalavāpisaṇṭhānaṃ titthameva vuccati. Payāgāti etampi gaṅgāya ekaṃ titthameva mahāpanādassa rañño gaṅgāyaṃ nimuggapāsādassa sopānasammukhaṭṭhānaṃ, bāhukā sundarikā sarassatī bāhumatīti imā pana catasso nadiyo. Bāloti duppañño. Pakkhandoti pavisanto. Na sujjhatīti kilesasuddhiṃ na pāpuṇāti, kevalaṃ rajojallameva pavāheti.

Therein, 'Adhikakkaṃ' is said to be a certain ford that received its designation by reason of bathing requisites. 'Gayā' too is said to be a ford with the shape of a circular or square tank. This name 'Payāgā' is also a certain ford on the Gaṅgā, the place facing the stairway of the submerged palace of King Mahāpanāda in the Gaṅgā. But these four—Bāhukā, Sundarikā, Sarassatī, and Bāhumatī—are rivers. 'Bālo' means one without wisdom. 'Pakkhandoti' means entering. 'Na sujjhati' means one does not attain purification from defilements; one only washes away dust and grime.

Kiṃ sundarikā karissatīti sundarikā kilesavisodhane kiṃ karissati? Na kiñci kātuṃ samatthāti adhippāyo. Esa nayo payāgabāhukāsu. Imehi ca tīhi padehi vuttehi itarānipi cattāri lakkhaṇāhāranayena vuttāneva honti, tasmā yatheva sundarikā payāgā [M 1.0183] bāhukā na kiñci karonti, tathā adhikakkādayopīti veditabbā.

'What will Sundarikā do?' means: In the cleansing of defilements, what can the Sundarikā river do? The intention is: it is not able to accomplish anything. This same method applies to the Payāga ford and the Bāhukā river. And when these three terms—Sundarikā, Payāga, Bāhukā—are stated, the other four terms are also stated by the method of implication from a characteristic. Therefore, it should be known that just as the Sundarikā, Payāga, and Bāhukā cannot accomplish anything, so too the Adhikakka and others cannot accomplish anything.

Verinti pāṇātipātādipañcaverasamannāgataṃ. Katakibbisanti kataluddakammaṃ. Na hi naṃ sodhayeti sundarikā vā payāgā vā bāhukā vā na sodhaye, na sodhetīti vuttaṃ hoti. Pāpakamminanti pāpakehi verakibbisakammehi yuttaṃ, lāmakakamme yuttaṃ vā verakibbisabhāvaṃ appattehi khuddakehipi pāpehi yuttanti vuttaṃ hoti.

'Veri' refers to a person endowed with the five enmities beginning with the destruction of life. 'Katakibbisaṃ' refers to one who has done a cruel deed. 'Na hi naṃ sodhaye' means: these fords and rivers—that is, Sundarikā, Payāga, or Bāhukā—cannot cleanse him. This is what is meant. 'Pāpakamminaṃ' refers to a person endowed with evil deeds of enmity and wickedness. Or alternatively, it refers to a person endowed with base deeds, endowed with minor evils that have not reached the state of enmity and wickedness. This is what is meant.

Suddhassāti [P 1.0179] nikkilesassa. Sadā phaggūti niccampi phaggunīnakkhattameva. Phaggunamāse kira “uttaraphaggunadivase yo nhāyati, so saṃvaccharaṃ katapāpaṃ sodhetī”ti evaṃ diṭṭhiko so brāhmaṇo, tenassa bhagavā taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭihananto āha “suddhassa ve sadā phaggū”ti. Nikkilesassa niccaṃ phaggunīnakkhattaṃ, itaro kiṃ sujjhatīti? Uposatho sadāti suddhassa ca cātuddasapannarasādīsu uposathaṅgāni asamādiyatopi niccameva uposatho. Suddhassa sucikammassāti nikkilesatāya suddhassa sucīhi ca kāyakammādīhi samannāgatassa. Sadā sampajjate vatanti īdisassa ca kusalūpasañhitaṃ vatasamādānampi niccaṃ sampannameva hotīti. Idheva sināhīti imasmiṃyeva mama sāsane sināhi. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? “Sace ajjhattikakilesamalappavāhanaṃ icchasi, idheva mama sāsane aṭṭhaṅgikamaggasalilena sināhi, aññatra hi idaṃ natthī”ti.

'Suddhassa' means: for the person without defilements. 'Sadā phaggu' means: it is always the Phagguna constellation. That brahmin held such a wrong view as this: 'It is said that in the month of Phagguna, whoever bathes on the day of the Uttaraphaggunī constellation cleanses the evil done for a whole year.' Therefore, the Blessed One, wishing to refute that wrong view of his, said, 'Suddhassa ve sadā phaggu.' This means: for a person free from defilements, it is always the Phagguna constellation; how can another person—one who is pure by means of virtue and so on—be purified? 'Uposatho sadā' means: for a pure person, even without undertaking the factors of the Uposatha on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and other such days, there is always the Uposatha of the Noble Ones. 'Suddhassa sucikammassa' means: for a person whose mental action is pure due to being free from defilements, and who is endowed with pure bodily and verbal actions. 'Sadā sampajjate vataṃ' means: for such a person, the undertaking of observances connected with the wholesome, such as the ascetic practices, is always fulfilled. 'Idheva sināhi' means: bathe right here in my Dispensation. What is meant? 'If you wish to wash away the internal stain of defilements, then bathe right here in my Dispensation with the clear water of the Noble Eightfold Path. Indeed, this Noble Path does not exist elsewhere, in the systems of other wrong views.' This is the meaning that is intended.

Idānissa [V 1.0188] sappāyadesanāvasena tīsupi dvāresu suddhiṃ dassento sabbabhūtesu karohi khematantiādimāha. Tattha khematanti abhayaṃ hitabhāvaṃ, mettanti vuttaṃ hoti. Etenassa manodvārasuddhi dassitā hoti.

Now, by way of a suitable teaching for him, wishing to show purity in the three doors, he spoke the words beginning with 'Sabbabhūtesu karohi khemataṃ.' Therein, 'khemataṃ' means the state of being without danger, the state of being for the welfare of beings; it is said to be loving-kindness (mettā). This is what is meant. By this, the purity of his mind-door is shown.

Sace musā na bhaṇasīti etenassa vacīdvārasuddhi. Sace pāṇaṃ na hiṃsasi sace adinnaṃ nādiyasīti etehi kāyadvārasuddhi. Saddahāno amaccharīti etehi pana naṃ evaṃ parisuddhadvāraṃ saddhāsampadāya cāgasampadāya ca niyojesi. Kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā, udapānopi te gayāti ayaṃ pana upaḍḍhagāthā, sace sabbabhūtesu khemataṃ karissasi, musā na bhaṇissasi, pāṇaṃ na hanissasi, adinnaṃ nādiyissasi, saddhahāno amaccharī bhavissasi, kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā udapānopi te gayā[M 1.0184], gayāyapi hi te nhāyantassa udapānepi imāya eva paṭipattiyā kilesasuddhi, sarīramalasuddhi pana ubhayattha samāti evaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Yasmā ca loke gayā sammatatarā, tasmā tassa bhagavā “gacchati pana bhavaṃ gotamo bāhuka”nti puṭṭhopi “kiṃ kāhasi bāhukaṃ gantvā”ti avatvā “kiṃ kāhasi gayaṃ gantvā”ti āhāti veditabbo.

By this phrase, 'If you do not speak falsely,' the purity of his speech-door is shown. By these phrases, 'If you do not harm living beings' and 'If you do not take what is not given,' purity in the body-door is shown. But by these words, 'Being faithful and un-miserly,' he urged that brahmin, whose doors were thus purified, toward the accomplishment of faith and the accomplishment of generosity. This verse, 'What will you do by going to Gayā? Even a well is Gayā for you,' is a half-verse. The meaning should be connected thus: If you practice safety toward all beings, do not speak falsely, do not kill living beings, do not take what is not given, and are faithful and un-miserly, what will you accomplish by going to Gayā? For you, even a well is Gayā. Indeed, for you who are bathing either at the Gayā ford or in a well, what purification of defilements can you accomplish by this practice of bathing? But the purification of bodily grime is equal in both places. And because in the world Gayā is more highly designated as a place for washing away evil, therefore the Blessed One, although asked, 'Does the venerable Gotama go to the Bāhukā?', did not say, 'What will you do by going to the Bāhukā?' but said, 'What will you do by going to Gayā?'. Thus it should be understood.

80. Evaṃ vutteti evamādi bhayabherave vuttattā pākaṭameva. Eko vūpakaṭṭhotiādīsu pana eko kāyavivekena[P 1.0180]. Vūpakaṭṭho cittavivekena. Appamatto kammaṭṭhāne sati avijahanena. Ātāpī kāyikacetasikavīriyasaṅkhātena ātāpena. Pahitatto kāye ca jīvite ca anapekkhatāya. Viharanto aññatarairiyāpathavihārena. Nacirassevāti pabbajjaṃ upādāya vuccati. Kulaputtāti duvidhā kulaputtā jātikulaputtā ca ācārakulaputtā ca, ayaṃ pana ubhayathāpi kulaputto. Agārasmāti gharā. Agārassa hitaṃ agāriyaṃ, kasigorakkhādikuṭumbaposanakammaṃ vuccati, natthi ettha agāriyanti anagāriyaṃ, pabbajjāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Pabbajantīti upagacchanti upasaṅkamanti. Tadanuttaranti taṃ anuttaraṃ. Brahmacariyapariyosānanti maggabrahmacariyassa pariyosānaṃ, arahattaphalanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tassa hi atthāya kulaputtā pabbajanti. Diṭṭheva dhammeti tasmiṃyeva attabhāve. Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvāti attanāyeva paññāya paccakkhaṃ katvā, aparappaccayaṃ katvāti attho. Upasampajja vihāsīti pāpuṇitvā sampādetvā vihāsīti, evaṃ viharanto ca khīṇā jāti…pe… abbhaññāsi. Etenassa paccavekkhaṇabhūmiṃ dasseti.

80. 'Evaṃ vuttaṃ' (Thus it was said) and so on: this is clear because it has been stated in the Bhayabherava Sutta. In the phrases 'eko vūpakaṭṭho' (alone, secluded), etc.: 'eko' (alone) means by way of physical seclusion; 'vūpakaṭṭho' (secluded) means by way of mental seclusion. 'Appamatto' (diligent) means by not abandoning mindfulness on the meditation subject. 'Ātāpī' (ardent) means by the ardour known as bodily and mental energy. 'Pahitatto' (resolute) means by being unconcerned about the body and life. 'Viharanto' (dwelling) means by dwelling in a certain posture. 'Nacirasseva' (before long) is said with reference to the going forth. 'Kulaputta' (son of a good family) refers to two kinds of sons of a good family: those by birth and those by conduct; but this one is a son of a good family in both respects. 'Agārasmā' (from the household) means from the home. 'Agāriyaṃ' (household life) refers to the work of supporting a family, such as farming and cattle-tending. 'Anagāriyaṃ' (the homeless life) means the absence of such household life; this is a designation for the going forth. 'Pabbajanti' (they go forth) means they approach, they draw near. 'Tadanuttaraṃ' (that unsurpassed) means that which is supreme. 'Brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ' (the culmination of the holy life) means the culmination of the path of the holy life; it is said to be the fruit of Arahantship. It is for the sake of this that sons of good families go forth. 'Diṭṭheva dhamme' (in this very life) means in this very existence. 'Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā' (having realized for oneself by direct knowledge) means having realized it directly through one's own wisdom, that is, without reliance on another. 'Upasampajja vihāsī' (having attained, he dwelled) means having reached and accomplished it, he dwelled. And dwelling thus, he fully knew: 'Birth is destroyed... [and so on].' By this, the stage of his reviewing knowledge is shown.

Katamā [V 1.0189] panassa jāti khīṇā? Kathañca naṃ abbhaññāsīti? Vuccate, kāmañcetaṃ bhayabheravepi vuttaṃ, tathāpi naṃ idha paṭhamapurisavasena yojanānayassa dassanatthaṃ puna saṅkhepato bhaṇāma. Na tāvassa atītā jāti khīṇā, pubbeva khīṇattā. Na anāgatā, tattha vāyāmābhāvato. Na paccuppannā, vijjamānattā. Maggassa pana abhāvitattā yā uppajjeyya ekacatupañcavokārabhavesu ekacatupañcakkhandhappabhedā jāti, sā maggassa bhāvitattā anuppādadhammataṃ āpajjanena khīṇā, taṃ so maggabhāvanāya pahīnakilese paccavekkhitvā kilesābhāve vijjamānampi kammaṃ āyatiṃ appaṭisandhikaṃ hotīti jānanto jānāti.

But what birth of his is destroyed? And how did he fully know it? It is said: Although this has been stated in the Bhayabherava Sutta, we will nevertheless state it again here in brief to demonstrate the method of application with reference to the first person. His past birth is not the one destroyed, since it was already destroyed before. Not a future birth, because there is no effort directed towards it. Not the present birth, since it is still existing. But whatever birth might have arisen—a birth distinguished as one, four, or five aggregates in the one, four, or five-constituent existences—that birth, because the path has been developed, is destroyed by attaining the state of non-arising. Having reviewed the defilements abandoned through the development of the path, he knows, understanding that in the absence of defilements, even existing kamma will not lead to future rebirth.

Vusitanti [M 1.0185] vutthaṃ parivutthaṃ, kataṃ caritaṃ niṭṭhāpitanti attho. Brahmacariyanti maggabrahmacariyaṃ. Kataṃ karaṇīyanti catūsu saccesu catūhi maggehi pariññāpahānasacchikiriyabhāvanāvasena soḷasavidhampi kiccaṃ niṭṭhāpitanti attho. Nāparaṃ itthattāyāti idāni punaitthabhāvāya [P 1.0181] evaṃsoḷasakiccabhāvāya, kilesakkhayāya vā maggabhāvanā natthīti. Atha vā, itthattāyāti itthabhāvato imasmā evaṃpakārā idāni vattamānakkhandhasantānā aparaṃ khandhasantānaṃ natthi. Ime pana pañcakkhandhā pariññātā tiṭṭhanti, chinnamūlako rukkho viyāti abbhaññāsi. Aññataroti eko. Arahatanti arahantānaṃ, bhagavato sāvakānaṃ arahataṃ abbhantaro ahosīti.

'Vusitaṃ' (lived) means lived, completely lived; done, practiced, finished—this is the meaning. 'Brahmacariyaṃ' (the holy life) means the path of the holy life. 'Kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ' (what had to be done has been done) means that the sixteenfold task regarding the Four Noble Truths—by way of full understanding, abandoning, realization, and development through the four paths—has been completed. 'Nāparaṃ itthattāya' (there is nothing further for this state) means that now there is no further cultivation of the path for this state, that is, for such a sixteenfold task, or for the destruction of defilements. Or alternatively, 'itthattāya' (for this state) means: from this state, from this present continuum of aggregates of this kind, there is no further continuum of aggregates. These five aggregates, having been fully understood, remain like a tree with its roots cut—thus he fully knew. 'Aññataro' (one of) means one. 'Arahataṃ' (of the Arahants) means he was included among the Arahants, the disciples of the Blessed One who were Arahants.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary on the Middle Length Discourses.

Vatthasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Vatthasutta is concluded.

8. Sallekhasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Sallekha Sutta

81. Evaṃ [V 1.0190] me sutanti sallekhasuttaṃ. Tattha mahācundoti tassa therassa nāmaṃ. Sāyanhasamayanti sāyanhakāle. Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitoti ettha paṭisallānanti tehi tehi sattasaṅkhārehi paṭinivattitvā sallānaṃ nilīyanaṃ, ekībhāvo pavivekoti vuttaṃ hoti. Yo tato vuṭṭhito, so paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito nāma hoti. Ayaṃ pana yasmā paṭisallānānaṃ uttamato phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhāsi, tasmā “paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito”ti vutto. Bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvāti samadasanakhujjalavibhūsitena sirasā bhagavantaṃ sakkaccaṃ vanditvā, abhivādāpetvā vā “sukhī bhava, cundā”ti evaṃ vacībhedaṃ kārāpetvā, bhagavā pana kira vandito samāno suvaṇṇadundubhisadisaṃ gīvaṃ paggayha kaṇṇasukhaṃ pemaniyaṃ amatābhisekasadisaṃ brahmaghosaṃ nicchārento “sukhī hohī”ti tassa tassa nāmaṃ gahetvā vadati, etaṃ āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatānaṃ. Tatridaṃ sādhakasuttaṃ, “sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatīti, sukhī hotu pañcasikha sakko devānamindo sāmacco saparijano, sukhakāmā hi devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā, ye caññe [M 1.0186] santi puthukāyā”ti. Evañca pana tathāgatā evarūpe mahesakkhe yakkhe abhivadantīti.

81. Thus have I heard—the Sallekha Sutta. Therein, Mahācunda is the name of that elder. 'In the evening' means at evening time. Regarding 'having emerged from seclusion,' herein 'seclusion' (paṭisallāna) means withdrawing from various formations of beings and settling into solitude, that is, being alone in seclusion. One who emerges from that is said to have emerged from seclusion. But this venerable one, because he emerged from the supreme of seclusions, the attainment of fruition, is therefore called 'one who has emerged from seclusion.' 'Having paid homage to the Blessed One' means having reverently bowed to the Blessed One with his head, adorned with the beauty of ten even, lustrous fingernails, or having caused him to be greeted with the words 'Be happy, Cunda.' But it is said that when the Blessed One is paid homage, he stretches his neck like a golden drum and utters a pleasant, lovely, nectar-like divine voice, calling each by name, saying, 'Be happy.' This is the custom of the Tathāgatas. Here is the supporting discourse: 'Venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, with his ministers and retinue, bows his head at the feet of the Blessed One.' 'May Sakka, lord of the devas, with his ministers and retinue, be happy, Pañcasikha. For devas, humans, asuras, nāgas, gandhabbas, and other diverse beings desire happiness.' And thus, the Tathāgatas greet even such great and powerful spirits.

Yā imāti idāni vattabbābhimukhaṃ karonto viya āha. Anekavihitāti nānappakārā. Diṭṭhiyoti micchādiṭṭhiyo[P 1.0182]. Loke uppajjantīti sattesu pātubhavanti. Attavādappaṭisaṃyuttāti “rūpaṃ attato samanupassatī”tiādinayappavattena attavādena paṭisaṃyuttā, tā vīsati bhavanti. Lokavādappaṭisaṃyuttāti “sassato attā ca loko cā”tiādinayappavattena lokavādena paṭisaṃyuttā, tā aṭṭha honti sassato, asassato, sassato ca asassato ca, neva sassato nāsassato, antavā, anantavā, antavā ca anantavā ca, nevantavā nānantavā attā ca loko cāti evaṃ pavattattā.

Regarding 'These views,' he spoke as if now turning to face what was to be said. 'Of various kinds' means of diverse types. 'Views' means wrong views. 'Arise in the world' means they appear among beings. 'Connected with theories of self' means connected with the theory of self that proceeds in the manner of 'one perceives form as self,' and so on; these are twenty. 'Connected with theories of the world' means connected with the theory of the world that proceeds in the manner of 'the self and the world are eternal,' and so on; these are eight, because they occur thus: the self and the world are eternal; non-eternal; both eternal and not eternal; neither eternal nor not eternal; finite; infinite; both finite and infinite; neither finite nor infinite.

Ādimevātiādīsu ayamattho kiṃ nu kho bhante ādimeva manasikarontassa appatvāpi sotāpattimaggaṃ [V 1.0191] vipassanāmissakapaṭhamamanasikārameva manasikarontassa bhikkhuno evametāsaṃ ettakeneva upāyena etāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānañca paṭinissaggo ca hotīti. Idañca thero attanā anadhimānikopi samāno adhimānikānaṃ adhimānappahānatthaṃ adhimāniko viya hutvā pucchatīti veditabbo. Apare panāhu “therassa antevāsikā ādimanasikāreneva diṭṭhīnaṃ samucchedappahānaṃ hotīti evaṃsaññinopi, samāpattivihārā sallekhavihārāti evaṃsaññinopi atthi. So tesaṃ atthāya bhagavantaṃ pucchatī”ti.

Regarding 'From the very beginning,' and so on, this is the meaning: 'Venerable sir, for a monk who attends right from the very beginning, even without having reached the path of stream-entry, by attending only to the initial attention mixed with insight, is it that by this much of a method alone the abandoning and relinquishing of these views occurs?' And this should be understood thus: the elder, although he himself was not conceited, asked as if he were conceited, for the sake of dispelling the conceit of the conceited. Others, however, say: 'There are disciples of the elder who perceive that the eradication of views occurs by the initial attention alone, and there are also those who perceive that attainment-dwellings are effacement-dwellings. He asks the Blessed One for their sake.'

82. Athassa bhagavā tāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānūpāyaṃ dassento yā imātiādimāha. Tattha yattha cetā diṭṭhiyo uppajjantītiādi pañcakkhandhe sandhāya vuttaṃ. Etesu hi etā diṭṭhiyo uppajjanti. Yathāha “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati rūpaṃ abhinivissa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati, so attā so loko so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.152) vitthāro. Ārammaṇavasena pana ekavacanaṃ katvā yattha cāti āha, yasmiṃ ārammaṇe uppajjantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Ettha ca uppajjanti anusenti samudācarantīti imesaṃ evaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Jātivasena hi ajātā jāyamānā uppajjantīti vuccanti. Punappunaṃ āsevitā thāmagatā [M 1.0187] appaṭivinītā anusentīti. Kāyavacīdvāraṃ sampattā samudācarantīti, idametesaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ. Taṃ netaṃ mamātiādīsu taṃ pañcakkhandhappabhedaṃ ārammaṇametaṃ mayhaṃ na hoti, ahampi eso na [P 1.0183] asmi, eso me attāpi na hotīti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passatoti evaṃ tāva padattho veditabbo.

82. Then the Blessed One, showing the method for abandoning these views, said, 'These,' and so on. Here, 'where these views arise,' and so on, is said with reference to the five aggregates. For it is in these that such views arise. As it is said: 'Bhikkhus, when there is form, by clinging to form, such a view arises: "This is self, this is the world, after death I shall be this—permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change"' (Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.152), and so on in detail. But with regard to the object, the singular is used in 'where,' meaning 'in which object they arise.' And here, 'arise,' 'lie latent,' and 'are enacted'—the distinction among these should be understood thus. By way of arising, those views not yet arisen, while they are arising, are said to 'arise.' Those repeatedly cultivated, strengthened, and not removed are said to 'lie latent.' Those that have reached the doors of body and speech are said to 'be enacted.' This is the distinction among them. In 'This is not mine,' and so on, 'this' refers to the object that is divided into the five aggregates. 'This is not mine' means this does not belong to me. 'I am not this' means I am not this. 'This is not my self' means this is not my self. Thus, one sees this as it truly is with right wisdom. This, then, is how the meaning of the words is to be understood.

Yasmā pana ettha etaṃ mamāti taṇhāgāho, tañca gaṇhanto aṭṭhasatataṇhāvicaritappabhedaṃ taṇhāpapañcaṃ gaṇhāti. Esohamasmīti mānagāho, tañca gaṇhanto navappabhedaṃ mānapapañcaṃ gaṇhāti. Eso me attāti diṭṭhigāho, tañca gaṇhanto dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhigatappabhedaṃ diṭṭhipapañcaṃ gaṇhāti. Tasmā netaṃ mamāti vadanto bhagavā yathāvuttappabhedaṃ taṇhāpapañcaṃ paṭikkhipati. Nesohamasmīti mānapapañcaṃ. Na meso attāti diṭṭhipapañcaṃ. Diṭṭhekaṭṭhāyeva cettha taṇhāmānā veditabbā. Evametanti evaṃ “netaṃ mamā”tiādinā ākārena etaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ. Yathābhūtanti yathā sabhāvaṃ, yathā atthīti vuttaṃ hoti. Khandhapañcakañhi eteneva ākārena atthi. Mamantiādinā pana gayhamānampi tenākārena nevatthīti adhippāyo. Sammappaññāya passatoti sotāpattimaggapaññāpariyosānāya [V 1.0192] vipassanāpaññāya suṭṭhu passantassa. Evametāsanti etena upāyena etāsaṃ. Pahānaṃ paṭinissaggoti ubhayampetaṃ samucchedappahānassevādhivacanaṃ.

Furthermore, herein, the grasping 'This is mine' is the grasping of craving; and in grasping that, one grasps the proliferation of craving, which is divided into one hundred and eight kinds of craving-wanderings. The grasping 'I am this' is the grasping of conceit; and in grasping that, one grasps the proliferation of conceit, which is divided into nine kinds. The grasping 'This is my self' is the grasping of views; and in grasping that, one grasps the proliferation of views, which is divided into sixty-two kinds of views. Therefore, the Blessed One, by saying, 'This is not mine,' rejects the proliferation of craving with its aforementioned divisions. By saying, 'I am not this,' he rejects the proliferation of conceit. By saying, 'This is not my self,' he rejects the proliferation of views. And herein, craving and conceit should be understood as having the same standing-ground as views. 'Thus this is' means: thus, by the mode beginning with 'This is not mine,' this pentad of aggregates. 'As it really is' means: according to its own nature, as it exists, is what is meant. For the pentad of aggregates exists precisely in this way. But even when grasped as 'mine,' and so on, the meaning is that it does not exist in that way. 'One who sees with right wisdom' means: for one who sees thoroughly with the wisdom of insight that culminates in the wisdom of the path of stream-entry. 'Thus of these' means: by this method, of these. 'Abandonment' and 'relinquishment'—both these are synonyms for abandonment by eradication.

Evaṃ bhagavā ādimanasikāreneva diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti nu kho noti āyasmatā mahācundena adhimānikānaṃ vasena pañhaṃ puṭṭho sotāpattimaggena diṭṭhippahānaṃ dassetvā idāni sayameva adhimānikānaṃ jhānaṃ vibhajanto ṭhānaṃ kho panetantiādimāha. Tattha adhimānikā nāma yesaṃ appatte pattasaññāya adhimāno uppajjati, svāyaṃ uppajjamāno neva lokavaṭṭānusārīnaṃ bālaputhujjanānaṃ uppajjati, na ariyasāvakānaṃ. Na hi sotāpannassa “sakadāgāmī aha”nti adhimāno uppajjati, na sakadāgāmissa “anāgāmī aha”nti, na anāgāmino “arahā aha”nti, kārakasseva pana samathavasena vā vipassanāvasena vā vikkhambhitakilesassa niccaṃ yuttapayuttassa āraddhavipassakassa uppajjati. Tassa hi samathavikkhambhitānaṃ vā vipassanāvikkhambhitānaṃ vā kilesānaṃ samudācāraṃ apassato “sotāpanno [P 1.0184] ahanti vā, sakadāgāmī, anāgāmī[M 1.0188], arahā aha”nti vā adhimāno uppajjati, talaṅgaratissapabbatavāsidhammadinnattherena ovādiyamānattherānaṃ viya.

Thus, the Blessed One—having been asked by the Venerable Mahācunda on behalf of those with overestimation whether the abandoning of views occurs by the initial application of mind alone or not, and having shown the abandoning of views through the path of stream-entry—now Himself, explaining the jhāna for those with overestimation, spoke the words beginning with, 'But this is a condition...' Herein, 'those with overestimation' are those in whom overestimation arises with the perception of having attained what has not been attained. This, when it arises, does not occur in foolish ordinary people who follow the round of the world, nor in noble disciples. For indeed, in a stream-enterer the overestimation, 'I am a once-returner,' does not arise; nor in a once-returner, 'I am a non-returner'; nor in a non-returner, 'I am an arahant.' Rather, it arises only in a practitioner whose defilements have been suppressed by means of either serenity or insight, who is constantly engaged and diligent, and who has undertaken insight practice. For when such a one does not see the occurrence of defilements suppressed by serenity or insight, overestimation arises, such that they think, 'I am a stream-enterer,' or 'a once-returner,' or 'a non-returner,' or 'an arahant,' like the elders who were being admonished by the Elder Dhammadinna, a resident of Talaṅgaratissa Mountain.

Therassa kira acirūpasampannasseva ovāde ṭhatvā bahū bhikkhū visesaṃ adhigacchiṃsu. Taṃ pavattiṃ sutvā tissamahāvihāravāsī bhikkhusaṅgho “na aṭṭhānaniyojako theroti theraṃ ānethā”ti sambahule bhikkhū pāhesi. Te gantvā, “āvuso, dhammadinna bhikkhusaṅgho taṃ pakkosāpetī”ti āhaṃsu. So āha “kiṃ pana tumhe, bhante, attānaṃ gavesatha para”nti? Attānaṃ sappurisāti, so tesaṃ kammaṭṭhānamadāsi, sabbeva arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Bhikkhusaṅgho puna aññe bhikkhū pāhesi, evaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ pahitā sabbepi tattheva arahattaṃ patvā vihariṃsu.

It is said that, though the Elder had not long been ordained, many monks who abided in his instruction attained a special distinction. Hearing of this, the community of monks residing at Tissāmahāvihāra, thinking, 'The Elder is not one to give improper instructions,' said, 'Bring the Elder,' and sent many monks. They went and said, 'Friend Dhammadinna, the community of monks summons you.' He replied, 'But why, venerable sirs? Do you seek another? Good sirs, seek for yourselves!' Then he gave them a meditation subject, and all of them attained Arahantship. The community of monks again sent other monks. Thus, up to the third time, all who were sent attained Arahantship right there and dwelt there.

Tato saṅgho gatagatā nāgacchantīti aññataraṃ vuḍḍhapabbajitaṃ pāhesi. So gantvā ca, “bhante, dhammadinna tikkhattuṃ tissamahāvihāravāsī bhikkhusaṅgho tuyhaṃ santike pesesi, tvaṃ nāma saṅghassa āṇaṃ garuṃ na karosi, nāgacchasī”ti āha. Thero kimetanti paṇṇasālaṃ appavisitvāva pattacīvaraṃ gāhāpetvā tāvadeva nikkhami, so antarāmagge haṅkanavihāraṃ pāvisi. Tattha ceko mahāthero saṭṭhivassātīto adhimānena arahattaṃ paṭijānāti. Thero taṃ upasaṅkamitvā [V 1.0193] vanditvā paṭisanthāraṃ katvā adhigamaṃ pucchi. Thero āha “āma dhammadinna, yaṃ pabbajitena kātabbaṃ, cirakataṃ taṃ mayā, atītasaṭṭhivassomhi etarahī”ti. Kiṃ, bhante, iddhimpi vaḷañjethāti. Āma dhammadinnāti. Sādhu vata, bhante, hatthiṃ tumhākaṃ paṭimukhaṃ āgacchantaṃ māpethāti. Sādhāvusoti thero sabbasetaṃ sattappatiṭṭhaṃ tidhāpabhinnaṃ naṅguṭṭhaṃ bījayamānaṃ soṇḍaṃ mukhe pakkhipitvā dvīhi dantehi vijjhitukāmaṃ viya paṭimukhaṃ āgacchantaṃ mahāhatthiṃ māpesi. So taṃ attanāyeva māpitaṃ hatthiṃ disvā bhīto palāyituṃ ārabhi. Tadāva attānaṃ “nāhaṃ arahā”ti ñatvā dhammadinnassa pādamūle ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā “patiṭṭhā me hohi, āvuso”ti āha. Dhammadinno “mā, bhante, soci, mā anattamano ahosi, kārakānaṃyeva adhimāno uppajjatī”ti [P 1.0185] theraṃ samassāsetvā kammaṭṭhānamadāsi. Thero tassovāde ṭhatvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

Then the Saṅgha, thinking, 'Those who are sent do not return,' sent a certain elderly monk. He went and said, 'Venerable Dhammadinna, three times the community of monks dwelling at Tissāmahāvihāra has sent messengers to you. Is it that you do not hold the Saṅgha's command in esteem, that you do not come?' The Elder, thinking, 'What is this?' without even entering his leaf-hut, had his bowl and robes brought and departed at that very moment. On the way, he entered the Haṅkana Monastery. There, a certain great elder, past sixty years in the order, was claiming Arahantship out of overestimation. The Elder approached him, paid respects, exchanged courteous greetings, and inquired about his attainment. The great elder said, 'Yes, Dhammadinna. Whatever is to be done by one who has gone forth, that was completed by me long ago. I am now past sixty years in the order.' 'Venerable sir, do you also wield psychic powers?' 'Yes, Dhammadinna.' 'Good then, venerable sir, please create an elephant coming towards you.' 'Very well, friend,' said the great elder, and created a great elephant, all white, firm on its seven limbs, with ichor flowing from three places, waving its tail, with its trunk placed in its mouth, coming towards him as if wanting to gore him with its two tusks. Seeing the elephant he himself had created, he became frightened and began to flee. At that very moment, realizing, 'I am not an arahant,' he sat down squatting at Dhammadinna's feet and said, 'Friend, be my support!' Dhammadinna reassured him, saying, 'Do not grieve, venerable sir, do not be distressed. Overestimation arises only in practitioners.' He then gave the elder a meditation subject. The elder, abiding in his instruction, attained Arahantship.

Cittalapabbatepi [M 1.0189] tādisova thero vasati. Dhammadinno tampi upasaṅkamitvā tatheva pucchi. Sopi tatheva byākāsi. Tato naṃ dhammadinno kiṃ, bhante, iddhimpi vaḷañjethāti āha. Āmāvusoti. Sādhu vata, bhante, ekaṃ pokkharaṇiṃ māpethāti. Thero māpesi. Ettha, bhante, padumagumbaṃ māpethāti. Tampi māpesi. Padumagumbe mahāpadumaṃ māpethāti. Tampi māpesi. Etasmiṃ padumagumbe ṭhatvā madhurassarena gāyantaṃ naccantañca ekaṃ itthiviggahaṃ māpethāti. Tampi māpesi. So etaṃ, bhante, punappunaṃ upanijjhāyathāti vatvā sayaṃ pāsādaṃ pāvisi. Therassa taṃ upanijjhāyato saṭṭhivassāni vikkhambhitakilesā caliṃsu, so tadā attānaṃ ñatvā purimatthero viya dhammadinnattherassa santike kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

On Cittalapabbata mountain, a similar elder also dwelt. Dhammadinna, having approached him also, asked in the very same way. He too answered in the very same way. Then Dhammadinna said to him, 'Venerable Sir, do you also use psychic power?' 'Yes, friend.' 'Venerable Sir, it would be good if you would create a square pond.' The elder created it. 'Venerable Sir, in this, please create a lotus bush.' He created that also. 'In the lotus bush, please create a great lotus.' He created that also. 'In this lotus bush, please create the form of a woman standing, singing with a sweet voice, and dancing.' He created that also. He, having said, 'Venerable Sir, please gaze intently at this one again and again,' himself entered the mansion. For the elder gazing intently at her, the defilements suppressed for sixty years were stirred. He then, having realized his own state, like the previous elder, received a meditation subject from the elder Dhammadinna and attained Arahantship.

Dhammadinnopi anupubbena tissamahāvihāraṃ agamāsi. Tasmiñca samaye therā cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ sammajjitvā buddhārammaṇaṃ pītiṃ uppādetvā nisinnā honti, etaṃ kira tesaṃ vattaṃ. Tena nesaṃ ekopi “idha pattacīvaraṃ ṭhapehī”ti dhammadinnaṃ vattā pucchitāpi nāhosi. Dhammadinno eso bhaveyyāti ñatvā pana pañhaṃ pucchiṃsu. So pucchitapañhe tiṇhena asinā kumudanāḷakalāpaṃ viya chinditvā pādaṅguliyā mahāpathaviṃ pahari. Bhante ayaṃ acetanā mahāpathavīpi dhammadinnassa guṇaṃ jānāti. Tumhe pana na jānitthāti ca vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –

And Dhammadinna, in due course, went to Tissamahāvihāra. At that time, it was the elders' observance, it is said, to sweep the cetiya courtyard and be seated, having generated joy with the Buddha as their object. Therefore, among them, there was not even one who spoke to or asked Dhammadinna, 'Place your bowl and robe here.' Dhammadinna knew, 'This must be their observance.' But they, having known this, asked him questions. He, having cut through the questions asked as if cutting a bundle of water lily stalks with a sharp sword, struck the great earth with his toe. And having said, 'Venerable Sirs, this insentient great earth knows the virtue of Dhammadinna, but you do not know,' he spoke this verse:

“Acetanāyaṃ [V 1.0194] pathavī, vijānāti guṇāguṇaṃ;

Sacetanātha kho bhante, na jānātha guṇāguṇa”nti.

'This insentient earth discerns the virtuous and the virtueless; yet you, Venerable Sirs, though sentient, do not discern the virtuous and the virtueless.'

Tāvadeva ca ākāse abbhuggantvā talaṅgaratissapabbatameva agamāsi. Evaṃ kārakasseva adhimāno uppajjati. Tasmā bhagavā tādisānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasena jhānaṃ vibhajanto ṭhānaṃ kho panetantiādimāha.

At that very moment, having risen up into the sky, he went to Talaṅgaratissapabbata mountain itself. Thus, the conceit of having attained the Dhamma of the Noble Ones arises only for one who strives in meditation. Therefore, the Blessed One, wishing to analyze jhāna by way of such monks, spoke the words beginning with, 'ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ'.

Tassattho, atthetaṃ kāraṇaṃ, no natthi. Yena idhekacco bhikkhu bāhiraparibbājakehi [P 1.0186] sādhāraṇaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihareyya, yaṃ pana tassa evamassa sallekhena viharāmīti, yaṃ paṭipattividhānaṃ kilese saṃlikhati, tenāhaṃ viharāmīti, taṃ na yujjati, na [M 1.0190] hi adhimānikassa bhikkhuno jhānaṃ sallekho vā sallekhapaṭipadā vā hoti. Kasmā? Avipassanāpādakattā. Na hi so jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā tato vuṭṭhāya saṅkhāre sammasati, jhānaṃ panassa cittekaggamattaṃ karoti, diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro hoti. Tasmā tamatthaṃ dassento bhagavā “na kho panete, cunda, ariyassa vinaye sallekhā vuccanti, diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā ete ariyassa vinaye vuccantī”ti āha.

The meaning of that is: that reason exists; it is not that it does not exist. Wherein, here, a certain monk—secluded from sensual pleasures, in a way common to non-Buddhist wandering ascetics—might dwell having attained the first jhāna. As for what might occur to him thus: 'I dwell by means of effacement'—that is, 'The practice which cuts away defilements, by that effacement I dwell'—that thought is not proper. For, indeed, for a monk with the conceit of having attained the Dhamma of the Noble Ones, jhāna is not effacement nor the practice of effacement. Why? Because it is not a basis for insight. For, indeed, that monk, having entered jhāna and emerged from it, does not contemplate formations. His jhāna merely produces one-pointedness of mind; it is a pleasant abiding in the here-and-now. Therefore, the Blessed One, wishing to show that meaning, said: 'These, Cunda, are not called effacement in the Noble One’s Discipline; these are called pleasant abidings in the here-and-now in the Noble One’s Discipline.'

Tattha eteti jhānadhammavasena bahuvacanaṃ veditabbaṃ, ete paṭhamajjhānadhammāti vuttaṃ hoti. Samāpattivasena vā, ekampi hi paṭhamajjhānaṃ punappunaṃ samāpattivasena pavattattā bahuttaṃ gacchati. Ārammaṇavasena vā, ekampi hi paṭhamajjhānaṃ pathavīkasiṇādīsu pavattivasena bahuttaṃ gacchatīti. Esa nayo dutiyatatiyacatutthajjhānesu. Āruppajhānesu pana ārammaṇabhedābhāvato purimakāraṇadvayavaseneva bahuvacanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Therein, 'these' should be understood as the plural by way of the jhāna factors; it means 'these factors of the first jhāna.' Or, it is by way of attainment; for even a single first jhāna becomes plural because it occurs through repeated attainment. Or, it is by way of the object; for even a single first jhāna becomes plural by way of occurring in relation to the earth kasiṇa and so on. This is the method to be understood for the second, third, and fourth jhānas. However, in the formless jhānas, because there is no variety of objects, the plural should be understood only by way of the two previous reasons.

Yasmā cetesaṃ aṅgānipi santāni ārammaṇānipi, nibbutāni ceva sukhumāni cāti vuttaṃ hoti, tasmā tāni santā ete vihārāti evaṃ vuttānīti veditabbāni. Ayaṃ tāva tesaṃ catunnampi sādhāraṇā vaṇṇanā. Visesavaṇṇanā pana “sabbaso rūpasaññāna”ntiādipadānusārato vattabbā siyā. Sā visuddhimagge sabbākārena vuttāyeva.

And because their factors are peaceful and their objects are both extinguished and subtle—this is the meaning—therefore they are called 'these are peaceful abidings'; thus they should be understood. This, first of all, is the general explanation for all four of them. The special explanation, however, should be stated in accordance with the words beginning with 'with the complete transcendence of perceptions of form.' That explanation has already been stated in all aspects in the Visuddhimagga.

83. Evaṃ [V 1.0195] yasmā adhimānikassa bhikkhuno jhānavihāro avipassanāpādakattā sallekhavihāro na hoti, na hi so jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā tato vuṭṭhāya saṅkhāre sammasati, cittekaggakaro diṭṭhadhamme sukhavihāro panassa hoti, tasmā tamatthaṃ dassento rūpajjhānāni ca arūpajjhānāni ca vibhajitvā idāni ca yattha sallekho kātabbo catucattālīsāya ākārehi, tañca vatthuṃ tañca sallekhaṃ dassento idha kho pana votiādimāha.

83. Thus, because for a monk with the conceit of having attained the Dhamma of the Noble Ones, the abiding in jhāna is not an abiding in effacement, as it is not a basis for insight. For, indeed, he does not, having entered jhāna and emerged from it, contemplate formations. It produces one-pointedness of mind, but for him it is only a pleasant abiding in the here-and-now. Therefore, showing that meaning, having analyzed the form jhānas and the formless jhānas, and now wishing to show the basis wherein effacement is to be practiced in forty-four aspects, and that effacement itself, He spoke the words beginning with, 'idha kho pana vo'.

Kasmā pana “aṭṭhahi samāpattīhi avihiṃsādayo sallekhā”ti vuttā? Lokuttarapādakattā. Bāhirakānañhi aṭṭha samāpattiyo vaṭṭapādakāyeva. Sāsane [P 1.0187] saraṇagamanampi lokuttarapādakaṃ, pageva avihiṃsādayo. Imināyeva ca suttena veditabbaṃ “yathā bāhirakassa aṭṭhasamāpattilābhino pañcābhiññassāpi dinnadānato sāsane tisaraṇagatassa [M 1.0191] dinnadānaṃ mahapphalataraṃ hotī”ti. Idañhi sandhāya dakkhiṇāvisuddhisutte “bāhirake kāmesu vītarāge dānaṃ datvā koṭisatasahassaguṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dānaṃ datvā asaṅkheyyā appameyyā dakkhiṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, ko pana vādo sotāpanne”ti vuttaṃ (ma. ni. 3.379). Saraṇagamanato paṭṭhāya hi tattha sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno adhippetoti, ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷiyojanā.

But why is it said that non-harming and the like are 'effacements' rather than the eight attainments? Because they are a basis for the supramundane. Indeed, for outsiders, the eight attainments are only a basis for the round of existence. In the Dispensation, even the going for refuge is a basis for the supramundane, what then to speak of non-harming and the like? And by this very sutta it should be understood that a gift given to one who has gone for the three refuges in the Dispensation is of far greater fruit than a gift given to an outsider who has obtained the eight attainments and the five supernormal knowledges. Indeed, with reference to this, it is said in the Dakkhiṇāvisuddhi Sutta: 'Having given a gift to an outsider who is free from lust for sensual pleasures, a reward of a hundred thousand koṭis is to be expected. Having given a gift to one practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, an incalculable, immeasurable offering is to be expected; what then to speak of a stream-enterer?' For here, beginning from the going for refuge, one practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is intended. This, firstly, is the grammatical connection of the Pāḷi here.

Anupadavaṇṇanāyaṃ pana idhāti vihiṃsādivatthudīpanametaṃ. Kho panāti nipātamattaṃ. Voti karaṇatthe sāmivacanaṃ, ayaṃ pana saṅkhepattho, yadetaṃ “pare vihiṃsakā bhavissantī”tiādinā nayena vihiṃsādivatthuṃ vadāma. Idha, cunda, tumhehi sallekho kātabboti.

But in the word-by-word commentary, this word 'idha' (here) indicates the subject matter of harming and so on. 'Kho pana' is merely a particle. 'Vo' is a genitive case ending used in the sense of the instrumental. But this is the concise meaning: That which I teach as the subject matter of harming and so on, by the method beginning with 'Others will be harmful,' is this: 'Here, Cunda, effacement is to be done by you.'

Evaṃ saṅkhepato vatvā idāni vitthārento “pare vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmāti sallekho karaṇīyo”tiādimāha.

Having spoken thus in brief, now elaborating, He said: 'Others will be harmful, but we here will be harmless; thus, effacement is to be done,' and so on.

Tattha pareti ye keci imaṃ sallekhamananuyuttā. Vihiṃsakā bhavissantīti pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vātiādīhi sattānaṃ vihesakā bhavissanti. Mayamettha avihiṃsakā bhavissāmāti mayaṃ pana yattheva vatthusmiṃ pare evaṃ vihiṃsakā bhavissanti, ettheva avihiṃsakā bhavissāma, avihiṃsaṃ uppādetvā viharissāma. Iti sallekho karaṇīyoti evaṃ tumhehi sallekho kātabbo[V 1.0196]. Sallekhoti ca idha avihiṃsāva veditabbā. Avihiṃsā hi vihiṃsaṃ sallekhati, taṃ chindati, tasmā sallekhoti vuccati. Esa nayo sabbattha. Ayaṃ pana viseso. Pare micchādiṭṭhīti ettha kammapathānaṃ antamicchādiṭṭhiñca micchattānaṃ ādimicchādiṭṭhiñca missetvā diṭṭhi vuttāti veditabbā. Tathā mayamettha sammādiṭṭhīti vuttaṭṭhāne sammādiṭṭhi. Ettha ca kammapathakathā vitthārato sammādiṭṭhisutte āvi bhavissati. Micchattesu micchādiṭṭhiādayo dvedhāvitakke.

Therein, 'others' means any who are not devoted to this effacement. 'They will be harmful' means they will be ones who harm beings with the hand, or with a clod of earth, and so on. 'We here will be harmless' means: we, in that very same situation where others will be harmful, right there we will be harmless; having generated non-harming, we will dwell. 'Thus, effacement is to be done' means: in this way, effacement is to be done by you. And here, 'effacement' should be understood as non-harming itself. For non-harming effaces harming, it cuts it off; therefore it is called 'effacement'. This is the method in all cases. But this is a special point. Here, in 'Others have wrong view,' it should be known that 'view' is spoken of by mixing the wrong view which is the end of the courses of action and the wrong view which is the beginning of wrongnesses. Similarly, right view in the place where it is said, 'We here will have right view.' And here, the talk on the courses of action will become clear in detail in the Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta. Among the wrongnesses, wrong view and so on will become clear in the Dvedhāvitakka Sutta.

Ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepo, pāṇaṃ atipātentīti pāṇātipātī [P 1.0188] pāṇaghātakāti attho. Adinnaṃ ādiyantīti adinnādāyī, parassa hārinoti attho. Abrahmaṃ hīnaṃ lāmakadhammaṃ carantīti abrahmacārī, methunadhammappaṭisevakāti [M 1.0192] attho. Brahmaṃ seṭṭhaṃ paṭipadaṃ carantīti brahmacārī, methunā paṭiviratāti attho. Ettha ca brahmacariyaṃ sallekhoti veditabbaṃ. Brahmacariyañhi abrahmacariyaṃ sallekhati. Musā vadantīti musāvādī, paresaṃ atthabhañjanakaṃ tucchaṃ alikaṃ vācaṃ bhāsitāroti attho. Pisuṇā vācā etesanti pisuṇavācā. Paresaṃ mammacchedikā pharusā vācā etesanti pharusavācā. Samphaṃ niratthakavacanaṃ palapantīti samphappalāpī. Abhijjhāyantīti abhijjhālū, parabhaṇḍalubbhanasīlāti attho. Byāpannaṃ pūtibhūtaṃ cittametesanti byāpannacittā. Micchā pāpikā viññugarahitā etesaṃ diṭṭhīti micchādiṭṭhī, kammapathapariyāpannāya natthi dinnantiādivatthukāya, micchattapariyāpannāya aniyyānikadiṭṭhiyā ca samannāgatāti attho. Sammā sobhanā viññuppasatthā etesaṃ diṭṭhīti sammādiṭṭhī, kammapathapariyāpannāya atthi dinnantiādikāya kammassakatādiṭṭhiyā, sammattapariyāpannāya maggadiṭṭhiyā ca samannāgatāti attho.

This is the summary here. Because they destroy life, they are 'destroyers of life'; the meaning is killers of living beings. Because they take what is not given, they are 'takers of what is not given'; the meaning is takers of another's property. Because they practice the unholy, base, evil thing, they are 'unchaste'; the meaning is indulgers in the act of sexual intercourse. Because they practice the holy, excellent path, they are 'chaste'; the meaning is abstainers from sexual intercourse. And here, the holy life should be known as 'effacement'. For the holy life effaces the unholy life. Because they speak falsely, they are 'speakers of falsehood'; the meaning is speakers of empty, untrue speech that destroys the welfare of others. They have divisive speech, therefore they are 'of divisive speech'. They have harsh speech that cuts others to the quick, therefore they are 'of harsh speech'. Because they prattle pointless, meaningless speech, they are 'prattlers'. Because they are covetous, they are 'covetous'; the meaning is one whose nature is to be greedy for another's belongings. They have a corrupt, putrid mind, therefore they are 'of corrupt mind'. They have a wrong, evil view, blamed by the wise, therefore they are 'of wrong view'; the meaning is being endowed with the view included in the course of action, which has as its object 'there is nothing given,' etc., and with the unliberating view included in wrongness. They have a right, beautiful view, praised by the wise, therefore they are 'of right view'; the meaning is being endowed with the view of ownership of kamma, such as 'there is what is given,' etc., which is included in the course of action, and with the path-view which is included in rightness.

Micchāsaṅkappāti ayāthāvaaniyyānikaakusalasaṅkappā. Esa nayo micchāvācātiādīsu. Ayaṃ pana viseso, micchāsaṅkappādayo viya hi micchāsati nāma pāṭiekko koci dhammo natthi, atītaṃ pana cintayato pavattānaṃ catunnampi akusalakkhandhānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Yampi vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthesā, bhikkhave, anussati, nesā natthīti vadāmi, puttalābhaṃ vā, bhikkhave, anussarato, dhanalābhaṃ vā, bhikkhave, anussarato, yasalābhaṃ vā, bhikkhave, anussarato”ti, tampi taṃ taṃ cintentassa satipatirūpakena uppattiṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ[V 1.0197]. Micchāñāṇīti ettha ca micchāñāṇanti pāpakiriyāsu upāyacintāvasena pāpaṃ katvā “sukataṃ mayā”ti paccavekkhaṇākārena ca uppanno moho veditabbo, tena samannāgatā puggalā micchāñāṇī. Sammāñāṇīti ettha pana ekūnavīsatibhedaṃ [P 1.0189] paccavekkhaṇāñāṇaṃ “sammāñāṇa”nti vuccati, tena samannāgatā puggalā sammāñāṇī. Micchāvimuttīti avimuttāyeva samānā “vimuttā maya”nti evaṃsaññino, avimuttiyaṃ vā vimuttisaññino. Tatrāyaṃ vacanattho, micchā pāpikā viparītā vimutti etesaṃ atthīti micchāvimuttī. Micchāvimuttīti ca yathāvuttenākārena pavattānaṃ akusalakkhandhānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Phalasampayuttāni pana sammādiṭṭhiādīni aṭṭhaṅgāni ṭhapetvā sesadhammā sammāvimuttīti veditabbā. Sā ca micchāvimuttiṃ sallikhitvā ṭhitattā sallekhoti [M 1.0193] veditabbā. Tattha niyojento āha “mayamettha sammāvimuttī bhavissāmāti sallekho karaṇīyo”ti.

“Those with wrong intention” are those with unwholesome thoughts that are misguided and do not lead to liberation. This same method applies to “those with wrong speech” and so on. Here, however, is a distinction: unlike those with wrong intention and similar states, there is no separate, single state called “wrong mindfulness.” Rather, this is a designation for the four unwholesome aggregates that arise for one who contemplates the past. As the Blessed One said: “Monks, there is such a recollection—I do not say there is not—whether it be recollection of gaining sons, wealth, or fame.” This should be understood as referring to the arising of what appears to be mindfulness when one reflects on those things. “Those with wrong knowledge” are those in whom delusion arises by way of contemplating the means for evil actions, or by reviewing evil actions with the thought, “I have done well.” “Those with right knowledge,” however, are those endowed with the nineteen kinds of reviewing knowledge, which is called “right knowledge.” “Those with wrong liberation” are those who, though not liberated, think, “We are liberated,” or who perceive non-liberation as liberation. The meaning of the word here is this: they have a wrong, evil, and perverted liberation, hence they are 'those with wrong liberation'. The term “wrong liberation” is also a designation for the unwholesome aggregates that arise in the aforementioned manner. However, setting aside the eight factors—such as right view—associated with fruition, the remaining associated states should be understood as “right liberation.” And because it stands having effaced wrong liberation, it should be known as “effacement.” Enjoining them in this, He said: “Effacement should be practiced with the thought, ‘Herein we shall be possessed of right liberation.’”

Ito parāni tīṇi nīvaraṇavasena vuttāni. Abhijjhālū byāpannacittāti evaṃ kammapathesu vuttattā panettha paṭhamāni dve nīvaraṇāni na vuttānīti veditabbāni. Tattha thinamiddhena pariyuṭṭhitā abhibhūtāti thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitā. Uddhaccena samannāgatāti uddhatā. Vicinantā kicchanti na sakkonti sanniṭṭhānaṃ kātunti vicikicchī. Kodhanātiādīni dasa cittassa upakkilesavasena vuttāni. Tattha kodhādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, taṃ sabbaṃ dhammadāyādavatthasuttesu vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha vacanattho – kodhanāti kujjhanasīlā. Upanāhīti upanāhanasīlā, upanāho vā etesaṃ atthīti upanāhī. Tathā makkhī palāsī ca. Issantīti issukī. Maccharāyantīti maccharī, maccheraṃ vā etesaṃ atthīti maccharī. Saṭhayantīti saṭhā, na sammā bhāsantīti vuttaṃ hoti, kerāṭikayuttānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Māyā etesaṃ atthīti māyāvī. Thambhasamaṅgitāya thaddhā. Atimānayogena atimānī. Vuttapaccanīkanayena sukkapakkho veditabbo.

From here, the following three are stated by way of the hindrances. Since “those with covetousness and a mind of ill will” are mentioned in the courses of action, it should be understood that the first two hindrances are not stated here. Therein, “those beset by sloth and torpor” are so called because they are assailed and overwhelmed by sloth and torpor. “The restless” are those endowed with restlessness. “The doubtful” are those who, while investigating, struggle and are unable to make a decision. The ten beginning with “the angry” are stated by way of the mind's corruptions. Therein, whatever should be said regarding anger and the like has all been said in the Dhammadāyāda Sutta. Here, however, this is the meaning of the words: “The angry” are those prone to anger. “The resentful” are those prone to holding grudges, or they have resentment. Similarly, “the contemptuous” and “the domineering.” “The envious” are those who envy. “The stingy” are those who are miserly, or they possess stinginess. “The deceitful” are those who practice deceit; it is said they do not speak truthfully—this is a designation for those endowed with craftiness. “The fraudulent” are those who possess deceit. “The obstinate” are so due to being endowed with stiffness. “The arrogant” are so due to excessive conceit. The bright side should be understood by the method opposite to what has been stated.

Dubbacāti vattuṃ dukkhā kiñci vuccamānā na sahanti. Tabbiparītā suvacā. Devadattādisadisā pāpakā mittā etesanti pāpamittā. Buddhā vā sāriputtādisadisā vā kalyāṇā mittā etesanti kalyāṇamittā. Kāyaduccaritādīsu cittavossaggavasena pamattā. Viparītā appamattāti veditabbā. Imāni [P 1.0190] tīṇi pakiṇṇakavasena vuttāni. Assaddhātiādīni satta asaddhammavasena. Tattha tīsu vatthūsu saddhā etesaṃ natthīti assaddhā. Sukkapakkhe [V 1.0198] saddahantīti saddhā, saddhā vā etesaṃ atthītipi saddhā. Natthi etesaṃ hirīti ahirikā, akusalasamāpattiyā ajigucchamānānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Hirī etesaṃ mane, hiriyā vā yuttamanāti hirimanā. Na ottappantīti anottappī, akusalasamāpattiyā na bhāyantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tabbiparītā ottappī. Appaṃ sutametesanti appassutā, appanti ca thokanti na gahetabbaṃ, natthīti gahetabbaṃ. “Appassutā”ti hi nissutā sutavirahitā vuccanti. Bahu sutametesanti bahussutā, tathāgatabhāsitaṃ ekampi gāthaṃ yāthāvato ñatvā anurūpapaṭipannānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Kucchitā sīdantīti kusītā, hīnavīriyānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Āraddhaṃ [M 1.0194] vīriyametesanti āraddhavīriyā, sammappadhānayuttānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ, muṭṭhā sati etesanti muṭṭhassatī, naṭṭhassatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Upaṭṭhitā sati etesanti upaṭṭhitassatī, niccaṃ ārammaṇābhimukhappavattasatīnametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Duṭṭhā paññā etesanti duppaññā, naṭṭhapaññāti vuttaṃ hoti. Paññāya sampannāti paññāsampannā, paññāti ca idha vipassanāpaññā veditabbā. Vipassanāsambhāro hi paripūro imasmiṃ ṭhāne āgato, tasmā vipassanāpaññāva ayanti porāṇānaṃ āṇā.

“Those hard to admonish” are difficult to speak to; they cannot bear anything said to them.
